examples.title: Anchored text
examples.summary: One word drawn at nine anchor points with every panX/panY combination of -1, 0 and 1; red guide lines cross at each anchor.
examples.prompt: In a canvas, draw the same word at nine anchor points with every panX/panY combination, with guide lines through the anchors, to show how drawTextAnchored aligns text.
teaches: Place canvas text relative to a point with drawTextAnchored(x, y, panX, panY)
Use panX -1 / 0 / 1 to put the text to the right of, centred on, or to the left of x
Use panY -1 / 0 / 1 to put the text above, centred on, or below y
Set the text's size and colour on the paint (textSize, color, style fill) before drawing

snippets.note: panX -1, panY -1: the anchor is the text's bottom-left corner
panX 0, panY 0: the text is centred on the anchor
panX 1, panY 1: the anchor is the text's top-right corner
paint for text: color, style fill, textSize 18

check.describe: Red guide lines cross at the nine anchors. The centre word is centred on its crossing; the top-left word sits above and to the right of its crossing, the bottom-right word below and to the left, and so on for each of the nine. Resized (200×300, 450×240) the guide lines stay at 1/6, 1/2 and 5/6 of the width and height and every word stays anchored on its crossing.

pitfalls: panX -1 puts the anchor on the text's LEFT edge (the text extends right), and panY -1 puts it on the BOTTOM edge (the text extends up): the pan says where the text goes, not where the anchor sits on it
panX and panY are required; json2rc refuses a drawTextAnchored without them, so write 0, 0 for centred text
Canvas text takes its size from the paint's textSize, and the paint is sticky: after a stroke paint, set style fill again or the text is drawn as outlines
Guide lines and anchors written as literal coordinates (50, 150, 250) only line up at the header size: derive them once from componentWidth() / componentHeight() as named variables and reuse them

examples.name: text-on-path
examples.title: Text on a path
examples.summary: A sentence that follows a sine wave built with pathExpression, drawn faintly underneath, nudged along and above it with hOffset and vOffset.
examples.prompt: Draw a sentence that follows a sine-wave curve, with the curve drawn faintly underneath.
teaches: Build a sine wave with pathExpression (x and y as functions of a[0]) and name it with id
Draw text along a path with drawTextOnPath(text, path, hOffset, vOffset)
Shift the text along the path with hOffset and off it with vOffset (negative is above)

snippets.note: pathExpression: x = 20 + a[0]*50.93, y = 100 - 45 sin(a[0]), a[0] from 0 to 2π, 96 points
drawTextOnPath on the wave, hOffset 12, vOffset -6

check.describe: The white sentence rises and falls with the faint blue wave, sitting just above it. Resized (260×200, 540×140) the wave spans the width less 20 on each side with an amplitude of 22.5 % of the height, and the sentence follows it.

pitfalls: Build the path with pathExpression (or the op-list path form) rather than an SVG string: Java pads a drawPath SVG string to ~4 KB, and an SVG string in resources.paths becomes an empty path
vOffset is perpendicular to the path and negative lifts the text above it; hOffset is a distance along the path, and text past the path's end is not drawn
Text on a tight curve bunches up on the inside of a bend: keep the curve gentle relative to textSize
A pathExpression with literal scale (50.93 per radian, centre 100) draws for one size only: use componentWidth() / componentHeight() in expressionX / expressionY

examples.name: number-format
examples.title: Number formatting
examples.summary: A live counter of the seconds since midnight, formatted by textFromFloat with 0, 1 and 2 decimals.
examples.prompt: Show a live number (seconds since midnight) formatted with 0, 1 and 2 decimal places.
teaches: Turn a live float into text with a textFromFloat value: whole digits, decimal places and flags
Compute seconds since midnight once, as a named resources.variables expression (timeInMin() * 60 + timeInSec() % 60), and reference it as @secs
Keep trailing zeros with flags 3 (PAD_AFTER_ZERO) and drop leading padding with 4 (PAD_PRE_NONE): flags 7

snippets.note: secs = timeInMin()*60 + timeInSec()%60, shared by the three lines
textFromFloat(@secs, whole 5, decimal 0, flags 7)
the same value with decimal 2: flags 7 keeps the .00

check.describe: At 10:10:05 the three lines read 36605, 36605.0 and 36605.00. Resized (240, 540 wide) the 80 dp label column stays put and the numbers keep their full width; at 240 36605.00 still fits.

pitfalls: timeInSec() is the second within the HOUR (minute*60 + second), not since midnight: at 10:10:05 it is 605
textFromFloat's default flags (0, PAD_AFTER_SPACE) print trailing zeros as spaces: 36605 with decimal 2 shows "36605.0" plus a blank; add PAD_AFTER_ZERO (3) to print 36605.00
`whole` is the number of integer digits KEPT, not a minimum: 36605 with whole 3 prints 605. Size it for the largest value (86399 needs 5)
Inside a text value object, decimal defaults to 3 when omitted; write decimal 0 for an integer

examples.name: text-lookup
examples.title: Weekday name lookup
examples.summary: Today's weekday name, picked at run time from a seven-name list with textLookup indexed by weekDay().
examples.prompt: Show today's weekday name ("Wednesday") picked from a list of seven day names.
teaches: Declare a list of strings with addDataList and give it an id
Pick one entry at run time with textLookup(array, index) and keep the result in varName
Index by the date: weekDay() is 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday), so weekDay() % 7 indexes a Sunday-first list

snippets.note: addDataList: seven day names, id days
textLookup(@days, weekDay() % 7) -> dayName
draw the looked-up text id like any other text, centred at componentWidth() / 2

check.describe: At 2026-10-28 (a Wednesday) it reads "Wednesday". Resized (190, 450 wide) the day name stays centred under TODAY.

pitfalls: weekDay() runs 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday): index a Sunday-first list with weekDay() % 7, a Monday-first one with weekDay() - 1
addDataList's `id` is a json2rc extension: the Java reference parser discards the list's id, so textLookup cannot name the list there and the document only converts with json2rc
Declare the list and the textLookup before the draw that uses varName: the name only exists from the textLookup on
examples.java_difference: json2rc-only: Java's addDataList drops the list id, so textLookup can't reach it (EXAMPLES_FINDINGS U4)

examples.name: multilingual
examples.title: Multilingual text
examples.summary: One line each of English, Japanese, right-to-left Arabic and emoji, all from plain text components relying on the player's font fallback.
examples.prompt: Show "Hello, world" in English, Japanese and right-to-left Arabic, plus a line of emoji.
teaches: Write any script straight into a text value as UTF-8: the player picks a fallback font per glyph
Let right-to-left text such as Arabic shape and order itself; no flag is needed on the component
Check a render for tofu boxes when a document mixes scripts

snippets.note: Japanese: こんにちは世界
Arabic, right to left: مرحبا بالعالم
emoji

check.describe: Four labelled lines; the Japanese, Arabic and emoji glyphs all render, with no tofu boxes, and the Arabic letters are joined and run right to left. Resized (270, 540 wide) the 64 dp label column leaves room for the 24 sp samples; at 270 こんにちは世界 still fits on one line.

pitfalls: Put the characters themselves in the JSON (UTF-8); there is no font or locale setting to make, and no escape is needed
Rendering depends on the player's fonts: a device without a CJK, Arabic or colour-emoji font shows tofu boxes, so check renders on the target
Right-to-left text runs right to left inside its own box but the box is still placed by the layout (start of a row is the left): the Arabic line here starts at the same x as the others
Japanese and Chinese have no spaces to break at: the C++ player keeps こんにちは世界 on one line and clips it when the box is narrower, so leave the sample enough width (a narrow label column)

examples.name: named-constants
examples.title: Design-token card
examples.summary: A card whose corner radius, spacing, chip size and four colours all come from named tokens in resources.variables and resources.colors, referenced as @name and @colors.name.
examples.prompt: Build a card whose spacing, corner radius and colours come from named design tokens instead of hard-coded numbers.
teaches: Declare numeric tokens in resources.variables and colour tokens in resources.colors
Reference a number token as @gap, or inside an expression such as "@gap * 4 + @chip"
Reference a colour token in a paint op as @colors.accent

Fit a drawing authored at the header size to any box: a variable s = min(componentWidth() / W, componentHeight() / H), a translate by half the extra space and a scale by s about the design's centre; the background drawRect runs before it, to componentWidth() × componentHeight()
pitfalls: resources.colors are exported (named, host-visible) by default, resources.variables are not: add "export": true to a variable only when the host should be able to change it
A token used in arithmetic must be written inside the expression string ("@gap * 3"), and each distinct expression becomes its own float op; reuse the same expression text rather than near-duplicates
A token is a host variable only when it is exported ({"value": 16, "export": true}); a plain number in resources.variables is a private constant the host can't see or change

Canvas coordinates are pixels of the box the host gives the document, not of the header: a background drawRect to the literal header size leaves the rest of a bigger box unpainted, and literal positions get cut off in a smaller one

snippets.note: radius, gap and chip sizes plus four named colours
card inset by @gap, corners @radius
paint color @colors.accent
second chip at @gap * 4 + @chip

check.describe: A dark rounded card inset 12 dp with a title and three blue rounded chips spaced 12 dp apart; the four colours are listed as named colours. Resized, the background fills the box and the drawing scales uniformly to fit, centred.

examples.hand_built: Built by hand in a canvas so every spacing, radius and colour visibly comes from a named token; library components such as Card read the theme's tokens for you.

examples.name: progress-bar
examples.title: Width-relative progress bar
examples.summary: A rounded progress bar whose fill ends at 16 + (componentWidth() − 32) × @progress, so it stays proportional at any width, with the percentage shown live.
examples.prompt: Make a horizontal upload progress bar driven by a 0..1 progress variable, with the percentage shown.
teaches: Size a shape from an expression that mixes componentWidth() and a variable
Expose the value as an exported host variable with a good default (0.65)
Show the same variable as a percentage with textFromFloat(@progress * 100)
pitfalls: Write the fill's right edge relative to the track (16 + (componentWidth() − 32) × @progress), not componentWidth() × @progress, or the fill overshoots the inset track

snippets.note: fill right edge: 16 + (componentWidth() - 32) * @progress
track spans to componentWidth() - 16
exported float progress, default 0.65
percentage via textFromFloat

check.describe: At the default 300 dp the fill is 65% of the track; at 500 dp with progress 0.3 the fill is 30% of the wider track and the label reads 30%. Resized, the track spans the width and the fill stays at 30% of it; the label and percentage stay at the two ends.

examples.hand_built: Built by hand to teach a size computed from componentWidth() and a variable; use the ProgressBar component for an ordinary progress bar.

examples.name: function-gallery
examples.title: Expression function gallery
examples.summary: Eight labelled mini-plots, one per expression function (sin, cos, clamp, lerp, step, fract, abs, pow), each a pathExpression over a[0] in −1..1, on cards laid out by a loop.
examples.prompt: Draw a cheat-sheet grid of small plots of sin, cos, clamp, lerp, step, fract, abs and pow, each labelled.
teaches: Call the expression functions with the argument orders RemoteCompose uses: clamp(min, max, x), lerp(a, b, t), step(x, edge), pow(x, n)
Plot each function as a pathExpression in a[0] (start -1, end 1), with y = baseline − height·f
Lay out repeated cards from a loop index with i % 4 and floor(i / 4)

Fit a drawing authored at the header size to any box: a variable s = min(componentWidth() / W, componentHeight() / H), a translate by half the extra space and a scale by s about the design's centre; the background drawRect runs before it, to componentWidth() × componentHeight()
pitfalls: clamp takes (min, max, value): clamp(x, -0.5, 0.5) clamps to the empty range and returns a constant
step(x, edge) is 1 when x > edge, so step(0, x) is the mirror image of the usual GLSL step(edge, x)
fract(x) is x − trunc(x), negative for negative x; shift the argument positive for a 0..1 sawtooth
flags 4 (LINEAR) joins the samples with straight segments; without it the path is splined and the step corners round off. A sharp jump also needs enough samples (count 201 here)

Canvas coordinates are pixels of the box the host gives the document, not of the header: a background drawRect to the literal header size leaves the rest of a bigger box unpainted, and literal positions get cut off in a smaller one

snippets.note: 68 - 56 * clamp(-0.5, 0.5, a[0] * 1.5): a ramp with flat ends
fract((a[0] + 1) * 2): four sawtooth teeth
pathExpression with flags 4 (linear segments)
eight cards from one loop: left 6 + (i % 4) * 88, top 8 + floor(i / 4) * 106

check.describe: sin and cos one period each, clamp a ramp with flat ends, lerp a straight line, step a jump at the centre, fract four teeth, abs a V, pow a cubic rise. Resized, the background fills the box and the drawing scales uniformly to fit, centred.

examples.hand_built: Built by hand to show each expression function drawn as a pathExpression; use the MathPlot component to graph formulas with axes and marked points.

examples.name: conditional-badge
examples.title: Conditional warning badge
examples.summary: A temperature reading from the host variable @temp that shows a red 'Too hot' badge only while @temp > 30, using conditionalOperations.
examples.prompt: Show a temperature reading with a red "Too hot" badge that appears only when the temperature goes above 30 °C.
teaches: Draw commands only when a condition holds with conditionalOperations {condition gt, v1, v2, commands}
Compare a host variable against a constant threshold (@temp > 30)
Show the live value with textFromFloat(@temp, 2 whole digits, 1 decimal)

Fit a drawing authored at the header size to any box: a variable s = min(componentWidth() / W, componentHeight() / H), a translate by half the extra space and a scale by s about the design's centre; the background drawRect runs before it, to componentWidth() × componentHeight()
pitfalls: condition is one of gt, ge, lt, le, eq for the Java parser; ne is a json2rc extension, and Java silently reads an unknown condition as eq. There is no else branch: add a second conditionalOperations with the opposite test

textFromFloat `whole` is the number of integer digits kept, not a minimum: with whole 2 a reading of 104 shows as "04.0". Pick `whole` for the largest value you expect; the °C unit sits at a fixed x, so leave room for that width

Canvas coordinates are pixels of the box the host gives the document, not of the header: a background drawRect to the literal header size leaves the rest of a bigger box unpainted, and literal positions get cut off in a smaller one

snippets.note: conditionalOperations gt @temp 30: badge drawn only when it holds
exported temp, default 24 (no badge)
textFromFloat(@temp)

check.describe: At temp 35 a red 'Too hot' pill shows beside 35.0 °C; at 20 (or the default 24) it is absent. Resized, the background fills the box and the drawing scales uniformly to fit, centred.

examples.hand_built: Built by hand to teach drawing only when a condition holds (conditionalOperations); use the Badge component for an ordinary badge.

examples.name: loop-grid
examples.title: Nested-loop dot grid
examples.summary: One hundred dots from two nested loops, each placed by its row and column and sized and faded by its index row × 10 + col, under a diagonal gradient paint.
examples.prompt: Draw a 10×10 grid of dots that grow and brighten from the top-left to the bottom-right.
teaches: Nest two loops with distinct index names (row, col) to cover a grid
Position each item from its indices: cx = 30 + col × 20, cy = 30 + row × 20
Vary a paint property per iteration with an index expression such as alpha 0.25 + (row × 10 + col) × 0.0075

Fit a drawing authored at the header size to any box: a variable s = min(componentWidth() / W, componentHeight() / H), a translate by half the extra space and a scale by s about the design's centre; the background drawRect runs before it, to componentWidth() × componentHeight()
pitfalls: The JSON has no per-iteration colour expression; vary alpha (or size) by index and let a gradient paint supply the hue
Give nested loops different index names: an inner loop reusing i shadows the outer index

Canvas coordinates are pixels of the box the host gives the document, not of the header: a background drawRect to the literal header size leaves the rest of a bigger box unpainted, and literal positions get cut off in a smaller one

snippets.note: outer loop row 0..9
inner loop col 0..9
alpha from the flat index row * 10 + col
diagonal blue-violet-red gradient shared by every dot

check.describe: 100 dots in a 10×10 grid, small and faint blue at the top left, large and bright red at the bottom right. Resized, the background fills the box and the grid scales to the shorter side, centred.

examples.name: array-bar-chart
examples.title: Bar chart from a float array
examples.summary: Twelve monthly bars drawn by one loop over a floatArrays resource, each height normalised by arrayMax so the tallest bar fills the chart.
examples.prompt: Draw a bar chart of twelve monthly sales values that scales the bars so the tallest one fills the chart.
teaches: Store a data series in resources.floatArrays and reference it as @sales
Loop over the series with until arrayLength(@sales) and read each value with arrayGet(@sales, i)
Normalise bar heights by arrayMax(@sales) so the chart rescales to any data
Derive the plot area from componentWidth()/componentHeight() so the chart stretches to whatever box the host gives it
pitfalls: resources.floatArrays are exported (named) by default, so a host can replace the series; the bar count follows arrayLength
Normalise with arrayMax(@sales) rather than a hard-coded maximum, or a host-supplied series with bigger values draws bars above the chart
Bar positions written against the header width (320 / arrayLength) leave the chart stuck at that width; measure the plot area from componentWidth()/componentHeight() instead

snippets.note: the 12-value series
loop i until arrayLength(@sales)
bar top: 180 - 160 * arrayGet(@sales, i) / arrayMax(@sales)

sales.meaning: the values to chart, any length

check.describe: Twelve blue bars; the eighth (41) touches the top guide line, the first (12) is under a third of the height. Resized, the chart stretches: the twelve bars share componentWidth() - 40 and scale to componentHeight() - 40, with the axis lines following.

examples.hand_built: Built by hand to teach looping over a float array and normalising by arrayMax; use the BarChart component for an ordinary bar chart.

examples.name: spline-curve
examples.title: Spline through control values
examples.summary: A smooth curve sampled from spline(@points, t) that passes through eight control values drawn as dots, beside a closed blob whose radius follows splineLoop over a second array.
examples.prompt: Draw a smooth curve through eight data values with the data points marked as dots, plus an organic blob shape.
teaches: Interpolate a float array smoothly with spline(@points, t), t from 0 to 1 across all values
Plot the spline as a path with pathExpression and mark the control values with arrayGet in a loop at x = i / (n − 1)
Make a closed organic shape from splineLoop as a polar radius, with pathExpression flags 1 (loop)

Fit a drawing authored at the header size to any box: a variable s = min(componentWidth() / W, componentHeight() / H), a translate by half the extra space and a scale by s about the design's centre; the background drawRect runs before it, to componentWidth() × componentHeight()
pitfalls: splineLoop only wraps t into 0..1 and evaluates the ordinary spline: repeat the first value at the end of the array or the loop has a jump at the seam
spline(@a, t) spreads the n values evenly over t = 0..1, so value i sits at t = i / (n − 1); place the marker dots at the same x or they miss the curve

Canvas coordinates are pixels of the box the host gives the document, not of the header: a background drawRect to the literal header size leaves the rest of a bigger box unpainted, and literal positions get cut off in a smaller one

snippets.note: a dot at each control value: arrayGet(@points, i) at x = 20 + i * 200 / 7
radius 25 + 50 * splineLoop(@blob, angle / 2π), closed path
points (8 values) and blob (first value repeated last)

check.describe: The blue curve passes exactly through all eight white dots with no corners; the violet blob is closed and smooth. Resized, the background fills the box and the drawing scales uniformly to fit, centred.

examples.hand_built: Built by hand to teach spline() and splineLoop in a pathExpression; use the LineChart or Sparkline component for an ordinary smooth chart.

examples.name: seeded-scatter
examples.title: Seeded random scatter
examples.summary: Two hundred dots whose positions and sizes come from rand() reseeded per dot with seed(n, rand()), so every render and every player draws the same scatter.
examples.prompt: Scatter 200 random dots of different sizes that look the same every time it renders.
teaches: Make random values reproducible with seed(s, rand()): it seeds the generator with s, then evaluates rand()
Give each dot and each coordinate its own seed (1 + i, 1001 + i, 2001 + i) so the result does not depend on evaluation order
Scale rand()'s 0..1 output into a range: 10 + 340 × rand
Spread seeded positions over componentWidth() - 20 by componentHeight() - 20 so the scatter fills any box
pitfalls: A bare rand() draws from the shared generator, so its values depend on what else has drawn from it and on evaluation order; seed inside each expression for a stable picture
seed(0, …) means reseed from the clock, i.e. not deterministic

snippets.note: 200 iterations
cx, cy and radius each from seed(k + i, rand())

check.describe: 200 dots of 1.5–5 dp scattered over the canvas, teal to violet left to right; two renders are pixel-identical. Resized, the same 200 seeded dots spread over the whole box (positions are fractions of componentWidth()/componentHeight()).

examples.name: component-values
examples.title: Layout from the measured size
examples.summary: Corner brackets, a centred disc and a live 'W×H' label all positioned from the canvas's measured width and height, captured once as @w and @h (COMPONENT_VALUE).
examples.prompt: Draw camera-viewfinder corner brackets and a centred size label that adapt to whatever size the widget is given.
teaches: Capture the canvas size once with variable {name: w, value: componentWidth()} (and componentHeight()) and reuse it as @w, @h
Pin shapes to the far edges with expressions such as @w - 12 and centre them with @w / 2
Scale a shape to the smaller side with min(@w, @h) / 4, and print the size with textFromFloat
pitfalls: componentWidth() is the size of the enclosing component after layout, not the document header size: the same document renders correctly at 200×200 and 500×300
A size label split into three texts (width, ×, height) needs the two numbers anchored away from the centre (panX 1 and −1) so the × stays centred whatever the digit count

snippets.note: variable w = componentWidth() (one COMPONENT_VALUE)
bottom-right bracket from @w - 12, @h - 12
disc at the centre, radius min(@w, @h) / 4
the width as text

check.describe: At 500×300 the four teal brackets hug the corners, the disc is centred with radius 75, and the label reads 500×300; at 200×200 it reads 200×200 with the same margins. At 300×450 (tall) the disc stays a quarter of the shorter side (radius 75) and the label reads 300×450.

components.name: activity-rings
components.title: ActivityRings
components.prompt: Show move, exercise and stand rings for today with their goals, with a second lap past a goal.
teaches: A short call: {"ActivityRings": {"rings": [{"label": "Move", "value": "@move", "target": 600, "unit": "kcal"}]}} in a sized box
Past a goal the ring runs a second lap, also in mono

snippets.note: rings, legend and centre on one canvas
one spoken summary of all rings
every length and sweep is an expression of the value and the box
numbers are rounded, formatted and fitted

check.describe: Three rings, blue, green and amber, 70% in the hole, Move, Exercise and Stand under them. move 1000: a second lap on the outer ring.

components.summary: Concentric activity rings, one to three, each a value against a goal, with a second lap past the goal, a centre number or a content slot, and values beside the rings when wide or under them when tall. Clear in mono; a screen reader hears one combined summary.
pitfalls: It fills the box it is given and arranges itself from that box: put it in a sized or weighted parent, with the padding on the parent. A near-square box of 240 or less shows the rings alone

Past the goal the first lap dims and a second lap runs over it, in the ring's colour; in mono the white ring carries a cut line. The ring wraps again at each further goal; the legend's numbers and the summary say the amount
In mono every ring is the same colour, so each legend row gets a small three-ring marker with its own ring drawn heavy. Keep rings outermost first in the order people read
The content slot centres on the whole box, so it turns the legend off: for a legend and a custom centre, use center and caption
Drawn text does not follow the system font scale. The spoken summary is English unless you pass description

components.name: adaptive-split
components.title: AdaptiveSplit
components.prompt: Lay out two parts side by side when the window is wide and stacked when it is narrow, and drop one when it is short, without copying them into a state layout.
teaches: Call it with slots.first and slots.second: one flow with exact cell sizes, so each part is written once instead of once per layout in a stateLayout
Give dropFirst or dropSecond a 0/1 expression of the window for what goes first when short

snippets.note: the two slots and when the second goes

check.describe: At 480x200 a primary square with 72 on the left half and the sentence on the right. At 360x480 and 240x240 the 72 band on top, 80 dp, and the sentence under it. At 320x100 only the 72.

components.summary: Two parts that sit side by side when the window is wide and stack when it is not, and that drop by priority when it is short: one flow, so each part is written once and not copied per layout. Decided by window size and never by content.
pitfalls: Each slot gets a box of exact width and height, so what is inside must fill or be smaller; give firstHeight for a part that needs a fixed height when stacked

A slot cannot read the split's values: the format has no way for a component to hand a computed value to its slot content. When content must follow the layout (a row count, a hidden caption), compute the same 0/1 flag in your document or a local, pass it as side, and read it in the slot
width and height default to the whole window. Inside padding, pass the window minus the padding: flow wraps as soon as the two widths exceed the real space
Weights do not reach through the flow: a part that grows must take the exact box (fillMaxSize)

components.name: allocationbar
components.title: AllocationBar
components.prompt: Show a portfolio's share per asset class as one rounded bar with a legend of names and percents.
teaches: Call {"AllocationBar": {"values": "@alloc", "items": ["Stocks", "Bonds"]}}: percents and lengths come from the array
legend none gives the bar alone for a widget

see the call
see the call
see the call

no second hand: hands are rotated lines
the twelve ticks are one loop

A clock that shows seconds repaints every second; without them, every minute

showDate draws dayOfMonth() as a two-digit textFromFloat (whole 2, decimal 0, flags 4: no padding) in a window at 3 o'clock, under the hands as on a watch; it reads the host clock, so pin `clock` to check a day
The twelve ticks are a loop that rotates the canvas 30° per pass (12 × 30° = 360°, back to the start), so the tick paint is set once and no save/restore is needed

A fixed `size` is the box the call asks for: a 160 dp clock still overflows a narrower widget. Where the space varies, pass fill: true and give the call a sized or weighted parent (weights ignore spacedBy: put the gap in a padding). Either way the face is drawn at `size` and a canvas variable (min(componentWidth(), componentHeight())) with one translate + scale fits it to the box it got, centred, so a call clamped by a smaller parent shrinks instead of being cut off; every coordinate stays a folded number. The variable keeps the call out of pattern mode, where min() over componentWidth()/componentHeight() comes out wrong (C++ and TS players)

components.name: avatar
components.title: Avatar
components.prompt: Round avatars with a user's initials on a coloured circle, in a few sizes.
teaches: Call it with initials: {"Avatar": {"initials": "AK"}}; size (default 40) scales the circle and the text
color picks the circle colour from the theme; the initials are onPrimary

snippets.note: a 56 dp avatar: a clipped round box
the default 40 dp size, primary colour

check.describe: Three circles left to right: violet AK (56 dp), blue JD (40 dp), green M (32 dp). Avatars are fixed-size circles in a start-aligned row: at 169 dp wide the three still fit, at 390 dp the row keeps its place and the rest is background.

components.summary: A round avatar showing initials on a colour.
pitfalls: Round by clipping to a rounded rect of radius size / 2: a `clip` circle shape writes nothing (Java and json2rc alike)

components.name: badge
components.title: Badge
components.prompt: A red badge with the live unread count, a "New" badge and a green "Beta" one.
teaches: Give count (a number or a "@variable") for a live number, or text for a fixed label
color re-colours one badge with a theme colour (default error red)

snippets.note: a live count from the exported @unread
fixed text with a theme colour

check.describe: A red 12, a red New and a green Beta; variables {unread: 3} shows 3. Badges size to their text: at 169 and 390 dp wide the three pills are unchanged and start-aligned.

components.summary: A small rounded badge holding a short text or a live count.
pitfalls: textFromFloat `whole` is the number of integer digits kept: whole 1 prints 12 as 2. Use enough digits with flags 5 (no padding before or after)
A badge over an icon is a box holding the icon and the Badge, aligned top-end; the badge is 20 dp tall and wraps its text

A count cap: {"count": "@unread", "max": 99} shows the number up to 99 and "99+" above (maxText), switched by visibility on the count; screen readers should still hear the real count from the item's own label.

components.name: banner
components.title: Banner
components.prompt: Show an info banner, an offline warning with a Retry action and a storage-full error that can't be dismissed, plus a Show all button that brings dismissed banners back.
teaches: kind picks the colour and the icon (info, warn, error); the icon's shape, not only its colour, tells them apart
visible is an integer variable: the cross sets it to 0 (the banner slides away, then the gap closes) and valueIntegerChange to 1 fades it back in
slots.action puts a short action before the cross; dismissible: false drops the cross

snippets.note: info: a 1.5 dp primary ring around a surface fill
bound to the int @offlineShown; Retry and the cross both set it to 0
error, not dismissible; the cross elsewhere is labelled Dismiss: <text>

check.describe: Three framed banners: blue info with a circled i, amber 'You are offline' with a triangle and a Retry action, red 'Storage almost full' with a circled ! and no cross. Tapping the info cross (x=300, y=72) at 0.1 s: 0.12 s later it is halfway out to the right (render-dismiss), and after the 300 ms exit the others have moved up into its place (render-dismissed). Resized, the banners fill the width: at 240 dp the messages wrap ('Sync finished: 12 new photos' takes two lines and the frame grows; the C++ renderer clips the wrapped offline message, which has a Retry action beside it, to its first line, C51; the TS player gives it its three lines), at 480 dp every message fits on one line.

components.summary: A one-line message in a rounded frame with an info, warning or error icon, an optional action and a dismiss cross: dismissing it slides it away and the space closes; setting its variable back to 1 fades it in again.
pitfalls: visible is an integer variable here ({"type": "int", "value": 1}, changed with valueIntegerChange) so the cross and the Show button set it directly; a float variable or expression that is exactly 0 or 1 also drives `visibility` (the player stores (int) value), so a computed condition works too

Dismissing slides it out to the right (exitSequence BEFORE) and then closes the gap; showing it opens the gap and then fades it in (AFTER). Components below it move smoothly only if they have an animationSpec of their own; otherwise they jump when the space closes
The frame is two stacked backgrounds (a 1.5 dp ring in the kind colour around a surface fill), not a border: border can't take a theme colour
In mono the kinds are told apart by the icon (circled i, triangle, circled !), since every colour is white; there is no slide or fade (mono has no motion)

components.name: bar-chart
components.title: BarChart
components.prompt: Chart weekly visits as labelled columns across a card, with a tiny steps chart next to the title.
teaches: Call {"BarChart": {"values": "@visits"}} with the name of a float array in resources.floatArrays; export it and the host can replace the data
labels: ["W1", ...] puts a short label under each bar (18 dp reserved under the baseline)
A fixed width × height (240 × 120 by default), or fill: true in a sized or weighted parent; the bars scale to 0..max of the data

snippets.note: bound to the exported float array visits
one drawRoundRect per value, in a loop over the array
84 × 28 without labels: a word-sized bar chart

check.describe: Eight blue columns labelled W1..W8 rising to 84 at W8, on a grey baseline filling the card; a small violet 7-bar chart beside the title, tallest on day 6. With variables {visits: [84, 69, 73, 58, 61, 48, 55, 42]} the big chart falls instead. At 234 and 540 dp wide the columns narrow and widen with the card.

components.summary: A column chart of a float array: one rounded bar per value from a zero baseline up to the largest value, scaled to the canvas, with optional labels under the bars.
pitfalls: values is the name of a float array ("@visits" declared in resources.floatArrays), not a JSON list: one loop draws every bar with arrayGet, so a host that sets the exported array redraws the chart, whatever its length
labels are text drawn when the document is built ($each over a list): a host can change the numbers but not the labels, so keep the array's length matching them
Bars are rounded at the top only: each is a drawRoundRect that reaches 4 dp below the baseline, clipped to the plot area, so the ends sit flat on the baseline
The scale is 0..max of the data, recomputed from the array: comparing two charts needs the same max, which this component doesn't share
Everything scales with componentWidth() and componentHeight(), read inline in each coordinate; it keeps the call out of pattern mode, which is fine for a chart drawn once or twice

components.name: battery-indicator
components.title: Battery indicator
components.prompt: Show the phone's battery level as a battery icon with the percentage, green when charged, amber at half and red with a warning mark when low, and a lightning bolt while it charges.
teaches: {"BatteryIndicator": {"level": "@battery", "charging": "@charging"}} draws a battery filled to an exported host float, with "76%" after it, and a bolt over the body while the host's charging flag is 1

The fill turns amber below warnAt (50) and red below lowAt (20) through conditionalOperations around a paint change, and low also draws a !, so mono shows it by shape; while charging the fill stays green and the ! is not drawn

The bolt is the library bolt icon (one shared path) drawn twice: a surface-coloured halo stroke, then an onSurface fill, so it reads over the green fill and the empty part; in mono the two swap (a black bolt, white-outlined over black)
size scales the icon (it is half as tall as it is wide); showPercent: false leaves only the icon

snippets.note: battery and charging, set by the host
bound to the host level and charging flag, with the percentage
95, 40 and 18 % in a flow: green, amber, red with a !
54 % and 5 % charging: a bolt over a green fill, no !
5 % charging: the bolt path (halo stroke, then fill) over the body instead of the !
72 dp, icon only

check.describe: The host level (76, not charging) gives a green icon about three quarters full and "76%"; the first flow shows 95 (green, nearly full), 40 (amber) and 18 (red, with a red ! in the empty part); the second flow shows 54 and 5 charging: both green with a dark (light theme) or light (dark theme) bolt with a thin halo over the body, and no ! on the 5. The large icon follows the host level. With battery = 15 (the low render) the first and last icons turn red and show the !; with charging = 1 (the charging render) they keep the green fill and gain the bolt. In mono the bolt is a black silhouette on the white fill and a white outline over the black empty part (the reverse in mono-light). The icons keep their size and sit in flows: at 240 dp the 18% one wraps to a second line, at 420 dp everything stays at the start.

components.summary: A horizontal battery icon filled to a level (0..100) and coloured by it (green, amber below warnAt, red with a ! below lowAt), with an optional percentage; while charging a lightning bolt sits over the body and the fill stays green.
pitfalls: There is no portable system battery level: batteryLevel() (system variable 38) is an rcj/json2rc extension that the Java parser rejects and Android's RemoteContext does not define. Export a host float (resources.variables {"battery": {"value": 76, "export": true}}) and pass "@battery"; the host updates it

The fill colour is chosen with conditionalOperations around a paint change (success, then warning below warnAt, then error below lowAt): there are no colour expressions. The comparisons read lc = lv + 100 * charging, so a charging battery is never below a threshold and keeps the green fill (and no !)
Low is shown by shape too: a ! in the empty part of the body, so it reads in mono (where every colour is white or black) and without colour vision

charging is a run-time value: the bolt sits in conditionalOperations (charging > 0.5), so a host variable can switch it. It is the library bolt icon (Material Symbols, rounded filled, one op-list path of about 0.5 KB shared by every call) scaled to 0.36 × size and centred on the body: a 90-unit stroke of the same path in the surface colour first (a 1.6 dp halo at size 40, so the bolt reads over the fill and the empty part), then the fill in onSurface. In mono the two swap (halo onSurface, bolt background): a black bolt on the white fill, a white outline over the black empty part

The accessibility label is a textMerge of label and ", charging" whenever the call passes charging; it cannot follow a host variable that is 0 at run time (a text id cannot be switched by a float), so bind charging only on an indicator that can charge, or pass a label that says it
The percentage is a layout text after the icon, so the call is as wide as the icon plus the number: in a tight row, pass showPercent: false and show the level elsewhere

The icon is scaled to the box the layout gives its canvas (the smaller of width / size and height / (size / 2), centred), so a call clamped by a smaller parent shrinks instead of being cut off; the outline stays theme.stroke wide at the design size and scales with it

components.name: big-number
components.title: BigNumber
components.prompt: Show this month's revenue as a big dollar amount with its change in percent, and under it costs in euros (lower is better) and active users abbreviated to millions, each with an up or down arrow.
teaches: Call {"BigNumber": {"caption": "Revenue", "value": "@revenue", "prefix": "$", "change": "@revenueChange"}}: the value is grouped by thousands (textFromFloat flags 23) and shrinks to fit its width, so 7 digits and more fit a half-width tile
grouping comma, period or space picks the separators (1,234.50, 1.234,50, 1 234,50); decimals keeps trailing zeros for cents; abbreviate shows 2.5M and 12.3K
The change is a drawn arrow and a signed percent in success or error (invert for costs), switched by paint alpha over step(change, 0): readable by shape and sign in mono

A screen reader hears one item, "Revenue this month, $1,284,530, up 4.2 percent": the canvas draws, an empty box over it after it carries the description, with the word cut from "updownunchanged" by textSubtext

snippets.note: a 7-digit dollar amount bound to an exported variable, grouped by commas
one description for caption, value and change
invert: a rise in costs is red; euros with space grouping and cents
abbreviate: 2,480,000 shows 2.5M, end-aligned
the down arrow, drawn with three lines

revenueChange.meaning: change since last month in percent

check.describe: Revenue this month $1,284,530 in 40 dp with a green up arrow and +4.2%; under it Costs 48 210,75 € with a red up arrow and +3.1% (invert), and Active users 2.5M end-aligned with a red down arrow and −1.4%. revenueChange −3 turns the first change red with a down arrow and −3.0%; 0 shows a muted flat arrow and 0.0%. Mono: the same arrows and signs in white (black on mono-light). At 240 dp the values shrink to fit their tiles; at 520 dp the end-aligned one follows the edge. A screen reader hears three items: "Revenue this month, $1,284,530, up 4.2 percent", "Costs, 48 210,75 €, up 3.1 percent", "Active users, 2,480,000, down 1.4 percent".

components.summary: A money or number KPI: a caption, a big formatted value (thousands grouping, a prefix or suffix such as a currency, decimals, optional K / M abbreviation, 7 digits and more) that shrinks to fit its width, and an optional change in percent with a drawn up or down arrow and its sign, green when good and red when bad. Read as one item: "Revenue, $1,234,567, up 4.2 percent".
pitfalls: Everything is drawn on one canvas (drawTextAnchored), so a screen reader hears one item: an empty box over the canvas, after it, carries textMerge(caption, value, "up" or "down", the change, "percent"). The word is cut from "updownunchanged" with textSubtext inside the canvas, which is why the description sits on a box after it: "@name" resolves only once the name is defined

Numbers are textFromFloat with flags 7 (no leading padding, trailing zeros kept so cents read .50) + 16 (group by three) + the separator style (64 period, 128 space): 23, 87, 151. whole is 9 digits; a float carries about 7 significant digits, so 12,345,678.91 prints as 12,345,679.00, and cents on 7-digit amounts are wrong (the C++ player draws 1,284,530.25 as 1,284,530.30 while the description says .25): show amounts of a million and more without cents (decimals 0) or abbreviated

The value is measured (textMeasure) and drawn under a scale of min(1, width / measured), so 7 or 9 digits shrink to fit a narrow tile instead of being cut off (StatTile stops at 6 digits). It fills its parent's width: in a row, give it a weighted box

abbreviate draws three texts (full, K, M) and shows one with paint alpha: k = step(|v|, 999.5) − m, m = step(|v|, 999999.5); the abbreviated number is value / (1 + 999 k + 999999 m) with one decimal, so 999,960 shows 1000.0K

The change line is three copies (the up arrow and +x% in success, the down arrow and −x% in error, a flat muted arrow and 0.0%) switched by paint alpha up = step(change, 0), dn = step(−change, 0), flat = 1 − up − dn; the spoken word (up, down, unchanged) is cut from "updownunchanged" with the same three. In mono both colours are white (black on mono-light): the arrow's direction and the sign carry the meaning
The prefix goes before the sign: a negative value with prefix "$" prints $-1,234; put the minus in your caption or use suffix instead
Drawn text has no bold and does not follow the system font scale

components.name: board
components.title: Board: a kanban of columns and cards, side by side or one at a time
components.prompt: Make a hiring pipeline board: Applied, Interview, Offer and Hired columns with a count each, cards with the candidate, a tag, an avatar and a date. Tapping a card moves it to the next stage. Show all columns on a tablet and one at a time with tabs on a phone.
teaches: Give columns as data, each {title, color, cards}, cards as {title, subtitle, tag, tone, who, due, late, value, id}. The component owns the rest: tabs or side-by-side columns, counts, scrolling, the move

Under 600 dp one column fills the screen under a tab strip naming every column with its live count; from 600 dp the columns stand side by side, 240 to 340 dp each, centred, scrolling sideways when they do not fit
A tap moves a card one column on: each card has an exported step variable and is written once per column, shown where its column plus its steps lands; the counts follow from one packed variable

snippets.note: the whole call: four stages and their candidates
a column: a title, a colour dot and its cards; a tap on a card moves it on
a card is one labelled tap target: its title, tag and column

check.describe: Phone: the title and Mobile team line, a tab strip Applied 3, Interview 2 and half of Offer, Applied underlined; three candidate cards with a tag, name, subtitle, avatar and date on a grey column. 640x360: three columns side by side and part of a fourth, scrolling sideways. 1280x800 and 800x1280: four columns with coloured dots and counts 3, 2, 1, 1. tap-move (wide): Priya Raman moved to Interview, counts 2, 3, 1, 1. phone-tap: after a card tap and the Interview tab, Interview 3 shows Priya Raman, Omar Haddad and Elena Petrova.

col.meaning: stage shown on a phone, from 0

board1_bM.meaning: moves out of each column, four bits per column

board1_bs00.meaning: columns this card has moved on (the app can read it)

board1_bs01.meaning: columns this card has moved on (the app can read it)

board1_bs02.meaning: columns this card has moved on (the app can read it)

board1_bs10.meaning: columns this card has moved on (the app can read it)

board1_bs11.meaning: columns this card has moved on (the app can read it)

board1_bs20.meaning: columns this card has moved on (the app can read it)

board1_bs30.meaning: columns this card has moved on (the app can read it)

components.summary: A whole kanban board from data: columns (To do, In progress, Done, or pipeline stages), each with a title and a live count, holding cards with a tag, a title, a subtitle, an assignee avatar, a due date and a value. From 600 dp wide all columns stand side by side (240 to 340 dp each, the board centred, scrolling sideways when they do not fit); on a phone one column fills the screen under a tab strip that names every column with its count. A tap moves a card to the next column (counts follow), and/or sends its id to the app.
pitfalls: Give columns and cards as data and let it decide, by the window width and never by content: under wideAt (600 dp) one column fills the screen under a tab strip (title and live count per column, the shown one underlined); from wideAt every column side by side, colMin to colMax wide (240 to 340), the board centred. When the columns do not fit (four at 800 dp, five at 640) the board scrolls sideways and the next column shows at the edge. There is no scroll bar
Columns hug their cards and scroll on their own once taller than the window, so a short column leaves the space under it empty, as on any kanban board

move (the default) writes every card once per column and shows the copy where it stands: about 1.2 KB per card per column (9 cards in 3 columns: 35 KB; 7 in 4: 37 KB). Keep a moving board to 15 cards and 6 columns (the counts are packed four bits per column in one float). For a big or app-fed board use move: false with action: each card is written once (about 1 KB) and the app moves cards and sends the board again

A tap moves a card one column on, never back, and the last column keeps its cards; there is no drag. A moved card takes its place in data order (cards from earlier columns first), not at the top. Where each card stands is the exported float boardN_bs<column><index> (columns moved), which the app can read

action is one host action name for every card, sending the card's id (its title if it has none) as a string. json2rc declares a name used by several cards once (Parser.ts EXTENSION); the Java parser writes it in the first card only, so the bytes differ from Java: say so in meta.java_difference. With move the action runs after the move and still sends the id, not the new column

A card: tag (one line), title (two lines, ellipsized), subtitle (one line), then a footer of who (24 dp Avatar), due and value. due and value are not ellipsized: keep them short ("Due Thu", "€140k"); late: true makes due red and bold, so it still reads in mono

Phone tabs are at least tabMin (112 dp) wide; a title must fit one tab with its count: about 11 characters ("Negotiation", "In progress"). The column variable chooses the phone's column and is ignored when wide
tone, whoTone and color are theme colours ("@colors.warning"), so dark and mono work. width and height default to the window: pass them when the board is not the whole window

components.name: button
components.title: Button
components.prompt: A pill-shaped primary Save button next to an outlined and a text button, one with a plus icon, a Submit button the host enables, and a full-width Sign in button.
teaches: Call it by name: {"Button": {"label": "Save", "onClick": {...}}}; the label is also the accessibility label
style picks the variant (filled, outlined, text); enabled: false dims it and drops the click
enabled can be a runtime 0/1 value ("@canSubmit", or an expression of resources variables): the button dims, ignores taps and is announced disabled while it is 0
fill: true makes it full width with the label centred (a form button)
A leading icon goes in slots.icon, about 16 dp, painted in the label colour (onPrimary on a filled button)

snippets.note: the minimal call: a label and an onClick action
a filled button with an icon slot
outlined style; every style is labelled from its label
enabled bound to the host variable canSubmit: tapping does nothing while it is 0
fill: true, a full-width button

check.describe: Five buttons in a flow: blue Save, outlined Edit, text Skip, a blue Add with a plus, and Submit, grey while the host variable canSubmit is 0 (a tap does nothing) and blue when it is 1 (a tap sets last to 5 and sends the host action submit); below them a full-width blue Sign in. Tapping Edit sets last to 2. At 234 dp the flow wraps to three lines (264 dp tall to hold it), at 540 dp all five stay on one line.

components.summary: A tappable button: filled, outlined or text style, with an optional leading icon, optionally full width. Labelled for accessibility from its label; enabled (true/false, or a 0/1 variable or expression read at run time) dims it, drops the click and marks it disabled. The 40 dp pill sits in a 48 dp tall touch target.
pitfalls: The outlined ring is two stacked backgrounds, not a border: `border` cannot take a theme colour (json2rc and the Java parser write the @colors id as a literal, transparent, colour). So the inside is painted with `surface`: set it to whatever the button sits on (@colors.surface in a Card), or the ring shows a background-coloured fill

The height is fixed: a 40 dp pill (control_height) with 4 dp (space_1) of transparent padding above and below, so the button is 48 dp tall and all of it is clickable; the clip and ripple stay on the pill. Leave no extra vertical space between stacked buttons or rows of buttons (the padding is 8 dp of the gap). The width wraps the label, so give a row of buttons room or they overflow; a label under about 16 dp (one or two letters) leaves the target under 48 dp wide
The label is one line with an ellipsis (maxLines 1): in a slot narrower than the label it ends in … instead of wrapping and being clipped by the pill

A runtime enabled ("@var" or an expression) writes the button twice, a disabled face and an enabled one, each shown by a visibility variable (enabled and 1 - enabled, computed from resources): only the enabled face has the click, ripple and onClick, so at 0 a tap runs nothing and sends no host action. It costs about 490 B more per call than a literal (plus the icon slot, written twice), so use a literal true/false when the state is fixed. The value must be exactly 0 or 1 and must read only resources variables (a host variable, an exported one), not a tree variable. A disabled face has no click to merge its text, so its label is on the text alone, marked disabled: one item for a screen reader, in both states. Its focus box is the text, not the pill
fill: true spans the width the parent gives (fillMaxWidth) with the label centred; in a row give it a weight instead or it takes the whole row

components.name: calendar-month
components.title: CalendarMonth: a month grid and the selected day's agenda
components.prompt: Make a personal calendar for November 2026: a month grid with today marked and the days with plans marked, and the selected day's events listed with their times. Tapping a day shows its events; on a tablet or desktop put the event titles in the day cells and the agenda in a side panel.
teaches: Call {"CalendarMonth": {"year": 2026, "month": 11, "days": [{"day": 2, "events": [{"time": "09:30", "title": "Dentist"}]}]}}: the grid, today, dots or chips, the selection and the agenda come with it
Phone: the month on top with up to three coloured dots per day, the selected day's events under it; a landscape window from 600 dp: big cells with the titles as chips and the agenda as a side panel
Omit year and month for the current month from the clock, and give weekly events (weekday 0 = Monday) that hold in any month; bind selected to read the tapped day

snippets.note: the whole call: a month and three days of events
a day and its events: dots or chips in the grid, rows in the agenda
a fixed month; today is marked while it is the current one (omit year and month to follow the clock)
stacked or side panel, dots or chips, chosen from the window size

sel.meaning: selected day of the month; 0 is today

check.describe: Clock 2026-11-02. Phone: November 2026 and Personal, Mon to Sun, the 1st under Sunday, 2 in a filled circle with three dots under it, one dot under 5 and 12, weekends grey; then Monday 2 November, Today, and four events with times and coloured bars. Landscape 640x360: same month left, the agenda as a panel right. Desktop and tablet: big cells, 2 outlined and tinted with the four events as chips (tablet: two chips and +2 more), Book club on 5 and Ana's birthday on 12. tap-12: 12 selected, the agenda shows Thursday 12 November, All day, Ana's birthday. mono: the same in black, white and grey.

components.summary: A whole month calendar screen from data: the month and year, weekday initials, a grid of 4 to 6 weeks with today marked, and the selected day's agenda. Compact cells (a phone) carry up to three coloured dots per day, large cells (a tablet or desktop) the events' titles as chips with "+N more"; a tap on a day selects it and lists its events. Stacked when portrait, the agenda a side panel from 600 dp wide in landscape. The month is a fixed year and month, or the current one from the clock.
pitfalls: Give the month and the events as data and let it decide: under sideAt (600 dp) or in a portrait window the month is on top (about 60% of the height) and the selected day's agenda under it; in a landscape window from 600 dp the agenda is a side panel (28% of the width, 260 to 360 dp). Cells from 64 dp wide and 60 dp tall show the events' titles as chips (as many as fit, then "+N more"); smaller cells show up to three dots in the events' colours. Decided by the window, never by content

Fixed month or the real one: year + month show that month (today is marked only while it is the current month, and the agenda starts on today or the 1st). Omit both for the current month from the clock, which rolls over by itself. Dated events (days) belong to a fixed month: the same day numbers in every month would be false. With the real month give weekly events (a class timetable, opening hours), or have the app rebuild the document each month

days: one object per day, {"day": 12, "events": [...]}; weekly: {"weekday": 0 (Monday) to 6, "events": [...]}; both can be given, weekly first in the agenda. An event is {"time", "end", "title", "subtitle", "color"}, only title required: no time reads "All day". Weeks start on Monday

Every event is written twice, as a chip or dot in the grid and as an agenda row (about 600 B for both), and each day with events costs about 250 B more: a full month of 20 events is about 30 KB. For a busy calendar fed by an app, keep titles short and leave subtitles out

Chip titles are cut at the cell's edge (a canvas cannot ellipsize): put the important word first. emptyText is drawn in one line under the day's events (they cover it when the day has any) and is not read by a screen reader: keep it under about 28 characters

selected is the day of the month, 1 to 31, and 0 means today (or the 1st when the month shown is not this month). Bind "@sel" to read it in agendaEnd (a Book button sending hostNamedAction with "value": "@sel") or to preset a day. Do not name a variable step

Each day of the month is a tap target written once (31 boxes in a flow after a spacer of the first weekday's width), announced as "12 November"; the grid itself is one canvas. Taps select; there is no swipe to another month
width and height default to the window: pass them when it is not the whole window. The month sits on surface, the agenda on background

components.name: callouts
components.title: Callouts: labelled parts of a drawing, placed for you
components.prompt: Label the parts of a drawing with leader lines, without working out where each label goes.
teaches: Call {"Callouts": {"aspect": 0.75, "parts": [{"at": [x, y], "label": "Shade"}], "slots": {"visual": [DRAWING]}}}: anchors are fractions of the drawing; the server places the labels and routes the leaders
Wide windows: labels in side gutters at least 8 dp apart, two-segment leaders that do not cross. Narrow: numbered discs and a legend (two columns when the labels are short). Tiny: the legend alone
The drawing gets a box of the exact aspect: scale a canvas from componentWidth() / 100 and draw in a unit box

snippets.note: the whole call: anchors, labels and the drawing; the look (beside, legend, legend alone) switches by visibility from the window size
the drawing slot: a canvas scaled from componentWidth()
label: what the drawing shows; each part label is read once

check.describe: A desk lamp: blue shade, yellow bulb, grey stem with a switch, a base. Phone: numbered discs 1 to 5 beside the lamp, joined by short leaders, and a legend Shade, Bulb, Stem, Switch, Weighted base. Landscape and tablet: the labels beside the lamp, Shade on the left, the others on the right, leaders not crossing.

components.summary: Labels the parts of a drawing for you: give the drawing (a slot), its aspect and each part's anchor as 0..1 fractions with its label; the server places the labels in side gutters with leader lines that do not cross (wide), or numbered markers on the drawing and a numbered legend below (narrow), and switches between them as the window changes.
pitfalls: Anchors are fractions of the drawing's box, not dp and not of the window: draw the visual in a unit box scaled from componentWidth() and divide its coordinates by the box size (x / 100, y / (100 / aspect)), or name them once in `points`
Whole window by default: inside your own padding or beside other content, pass width and height, or the drawing and labels come out too large

Labels are measured when the document is built: a label the host changes at run time is not supported. A gutter is at most 160 dp wide; a longer label wraps (3 lines at most), and in the legend 2 lines

Leaders do not cross while a side's labels need at most about twice the drawing's height, which auto keeps to: each side's order is chosen for it at phone, tablet, desktop and widget sizes, and a neighbouring pair whose leaders would still cross trades places at run time. A crowd of anchors on one side of a small drawing, with a forced mode, can still cross; spread the anchors over both halves, or give a part an explicit side

Narrow windows show numbered discs and a legend (two columns when every label fits half the width). When the drawing would be under 56 dp, or its discs would stack past 1.6 times its height, the drawing hides and the legend stands alone; a legend of many parts in a very small window (8 parts under about 200 dp tall) is cut at the bottom

Draw the visual with theme colours, never hex literals: a navy lamp drawn in #1E3A5F vanishes on the dark background and a pale ground line glares. Use @colors.onSurface for outlines and dark parts, @colors.surfaceHigh or @colors.outline for bodies, @colors.primary for one accent, and {"$if": "theme.mono"} (in an inline component) for an outline-only mono look, as CMP-30's CoffeeMachine does

Curves in the drawing: use drawPath with an op-list path ([{"type": "moveTo", "x": 65, "y": 29}, {"type": "quadTo", "x1": 81, "y1": 25, "x2": 88, "y2": 40}, {"type": "close"}] under resources.paths, or inline), not an SVG string ("M65 29 L81 25 Q..."): the Java parser pads an SVG string to about 4 KB per path. Rounded rects, circles, lines and arcs cover most parts

Everything it places (labels, discs, legend rows, the drawing's box and your drawing's top node) opts out of the players' 300 ms bounds animation (animationSpec 0), so on a resize labels and leader lines move together, at once. Nodes deeper in your drawing are not touched
The whole frame is expanded, never a pattern (texts and canvas). About 2.9 KB plus about 1.1 KB per part in .rc (both looks are in the document), before the drawing

components.name: card
components.title: Card
components.prompt: A rounded card with a title, a subtitle, a line of body text and two action buttons.
teaches: Call it with a title and subtitle, both optional; body content goes in slots.content (or children), buttons in slots.actions
The card fills its width and pads by 16 dp: components inside should not pad themselves again

snippets.note: title, subtitle, content slot and actions row in one call
the actions slot holds Buttons

check.describe: A rounded surface card titled Storage with a muted subtitle, a body line and Manage / Later buttons; tapping Manage sets action to 1. The card fills the width: at 234 dp the body line wraps to two lines and the card grows taller, at 540 dp it stretches with the buttons kept at the start.

components.summary: A rounded surface with an optional title, an optional subtitle, a content slot and an actions row.
pitfalls: `title` is optional: left out, no text node is written and the content starts at the top. A card with no title should still have something that says what it is, for a screen reader

The card fills its width and pads its content by 16 dp with 8 dp spacedBy: components inside that pad themselves (ListItem) should pass padding 0, and an outlined Button inside should pass surface: "@colors.surface"
The content slot is a column: a row of things side by side needs its own row (with weighted boxes, not spacedBy, if anything in it is weighted)

components.name: CellRow
components.title: CellRow: a list of numbers an algorithm works on
components.prompt: Show six numbers with two compared and the sorted part marked.
teaches: Each value and index an expression: {"CellRow": {"values": ["@a0", ...], "a": "@i", "b": "@i + 1", "swap": "@did", "doneFrom": "@sorted"}}; it fills its box
Light, dark and mono come from the same call; the demo's check.renders sweep the sizes

snippets.note: the call and its slots
the call and its slots
the call and its slots

check.describe: Cells 2 5 1 8 3 9 with 5 and 1 filled and bracketed with dots, 9 green; below it the same as bars.

components.summary: A row of numbered cells or bars for explaining an algorithm over a short list: it shows each value, highlights a pair (a, b) with a bracket, marks a swap, and fills the settled cells. Every value and index is an expression, so it follows a step.
pitfalls: No locals read its params, so a, b, swap and doneFrom may read a tree variable (the step a StepExplainer publishes), unlike TextChoice
Expanded per call, about 720 B per cell with numbers inside and 610 B per bar (6 cells 5.7 KB, 6 bars 4.9 KB)

bars ease only the fraction value / max, never a coordinate: an animated value starts from its first evaluation, and componentHeight() is 0 then, so an eased coordinate starts wrong and a first frame shows it
Fills the box it is given: 56 dp wide per cell or so reads well; the number shrinks with the cell

components.name: chart-3d
components.title: Chart3D
components.prompt: Show monthly rainfall for London, Seattle and Mumbai from January to June as 3D bars I can turn, and below it the saddle z = x² − y² as a 3D surface.
teaches: Data, not geometry: {"Chart3D": {"categories": [...], "series": [...], "values": [[...], ...]}} gives 3D bars; {"fn": "x^2 - y^2", "x": [-2, 2]} a surface; points [[x, y, z], ...] a scatter. The server picks round ranges and ticks and frames the camera
Floor and back walls carry gridlines on the ticks; the wall facing the camera is culled, so the back two always show as it turns
Labels are 2D text at projected points, computed at run time from the same spin and tilt as the 3D pass: they follow the orbit and stay sharp

Bars take the theme's series colours in a fixed order and a legend; a surface and a scatter take a five-step blue ramp by height (one mesh per step); mono draws boxes with edges and a hidden-line wireframe
pitfalls: 3D support has not landed in androidx yet (coming): Chart3D plays in the C++ and TypeScript players (rc2image, the web player, the MCP renders) only. Don't use it for a screen that must play on Android today
Give the data, not geometry: points, or categories + values, or a formula. Never compute positions, ticks or camera angles yourself; the server maps the data into the box and picks round ranges
Colour by value is five steps of one blue (light = low, dark = high), not a continuous gradient: each mesh takes one paint colour. Values in one step look the same; the legend shows the steps' range

A surface's colour bands follow its grid cells, so their edges are stepped at the grid's size; raise resolution for smoother bands (each step costs render time: five copies of the mesh are evaluated every frame)
A variable in a surface formula (vars) must be read after whatever writes it: put a Slider above the chart in the document, since a slider's live value is its own variable only from the slider on
Every mesh draw composites a window-sized buffer in the players, so render time grows with the number of draws: a scatter of 50 points is about 60 draws. Keep scatters under about 100 points

Labels are 2D text placed from projected points: tick values on the floor edges nearest the viewer and up a back corner, titles beyond them. At very small sizes (under about 180 dp) they crowd: give the chart room or drop the titles
Mono draws points and bars in the text colour with shading (bars as boxes with drawn edges) and the surface as a hidden-line wireframe; size and position carry the data, colour does not
3D support has not landed in androidx yet (coming): this plays in the C++ and TypeScript players only. Don't use it for a screen that must play on Android today
components.java_difference: 3D operations: not in the Java JSON parser or androidx remote-core yet; 3D support has not landed in androidx yet (coming); plays in the C++ and TypeScript players

snippets.note: bars: categories by series, one cube drawn in a loop per series
each series is one loop over a float array of positions and sizes
the bars' boxes are a float array the server writes
the formula becomes a mesh expression evaluated by the player
camera framed for the canvas at any aspect
drag to orbit
the description names the categories, series and highest bar

check.describe: Two 3D charts. Top: rainfall bars, six months across (Jan to Jun) by three cities into the screen (London blue, Seattle orange, Mumbai green), floor and two back walls with gridlines, 'Rain (mm)' 0 to 600 up the left; Mumbai's June bar towers at about 485. Legend London, Seattle, Mumbai. Bottom: the saddle z = x² − y² over −2..2, banded light to dark blue by height (−4 to 4), a grey skirt down its sides. Mono: bars as boxes with drawn edges, the saddle as a hidden-line wireframe.

components.summary: A 3D chart from data, not geometry: a scatter of points ([x, y, z], sized and coloured by value), bars (categories by series) or a surface z = f(x, y) from a formula. The server picks the axis ranges and ticks, draws a floor and back walls with gridlines, labels the axes from projected points, frames the camera for any aspect and lets the viewer drag to orbit.

components.name: chat-thread
components.title: ChatThread: a conversation with bubbles, anchored to the latest message
components.prompt: Make a chat screen with Léa: our messages about Saturday's hike as bubbles, mine on the right in blue, hers on the left, day separators, times, a read receipt, and a message field with a send button at the bottom.
teaches: Give messages as data, oldest first: {text, me, time, day, status, react}. The component owns the rest: sides, colours, wrapping at about 78% of the width (520 dp at most), day separators, the header and the composer
The thread is anchored to the bottom: the latest message shows above the composer and a drag down scrolls back to older ones (a short thread sits at the bottom, not the top)
RemoteCompose has no text input: the composer field is a tap target that asks the app for input (hostNamedAction compose) and shows the app's draft text; the send button sends hostNamedAction send

snippets.note: the whole call: a two-person chat, anchored to the latest message
messages oldest first; a drag down on the thread scrolls back to older ones
the composer field: a tap asks the app for input (hostNamedAction compose)
a call button in the header sends hostNamedAction call
each bubble is read as You: or the sender, then the text

check.describe: Phone: a header with the LM avatar, Léa Martin, online and a call icon; the end of the thread (the forecast, a thumbs-up under Perfect, Today, the train, sandwiches, thermos, my last bubble with Read 08:46) right above a Message field and a round send button. scrolled: dragged down, the start of the thread with Yesterday and the first question shows. Landscape: the last four messages, one line each. Desktop and tablet: the whole thread at the bottom of a 920 dp column centred, bubbles at most 520 dp, empty space above (a short thread is anchored to the bottom).

components.summary: A whole chat conversation from data: a header (avatar, name, status), the messages as bubbles (yours on the end side in the primary colour, theirs on the start side, with day separators, sender names, avatars, times, read status, reactions and attachments), the thread anchored to the bottom so the latest message shows and a drag scrolls back, and a composer row (a field that asks the app for input, a send button). From 720 dp a conversation list can show beside it.
pitfalls: Give messages as data, oldest first, and let it lay out: yours (me: true) on the end side in color, theirs on the start side on surfaceHigh, each bubble wrapping at bubbleShare of the thread (0.78) and at most maxBubble (520 dp); from listAt (720 dp) with conversations the chat list takes listWidth (320 dp) at the start; the thread is centred at most maxThread (920 dp) wide. Decided by the window width, never by content

The thread is anchored to the bottom: the latest message sits right above the composer, a short thread sits at the bottom with empty space above (as in every messenger), and a drag down scrolls back to the oldest. The scroll is the component's own (a touchExpression and a translation by the measured thread height), not verticalScroll, whose position always starts at the top

Render or record with a few frames (render_rc duration 0.5, or any touch): the C++ player computes the thread's height-based translation from the previous layout, so a single-frame C++ render shows the thread pushed out of view. The TypeScript player and a running C++ player are right from the second frame

Nothing inside the thread is tappable: the bubbles are moved at paint time, so a click target in an attachment would not be under the finger. Put actions in the header (headerEnd), before the field (composerStart) or in replies

There is no text input in RemoteCompose: the field is a tap target that runs onCompose (default hostNamedAction compose) so the app can open its own keyboard, and shows draft (a host text variable, "@draft") or the placeholder. The send button runs onSend (default hostNamedAction send). The app appends the sent message and serves the new document

Group chats: avatars: true indents theirs by 40 dp; give name on the FIRST message of a run of one sender and lead (an Avatar of size 32) on the LAST, as messengers do. Without avatars, lead is ignored

attachment is any node, drawn full bubble width above the text (a file or invoice card on @colors.surface); the bubble then takes its widest. react is a Material Symbols name (favorite, thumb_up) in a pill under the bubble, reactCount the number; status is the muted line under it (Read 09:42, Seen by ...)

replies are chips in a horizontally scrolling row above the composer; every chip sends the same hostNamedAction (replyAction, default reply) with its index, so json2rc and the Java parser write different bytes (json2rc declares the shared name once on purpose): record it as meta.java_difference

selected is the highlighted conversation (0-based, only with conversations): bind an exported resources variable ("@chat") to read taps; the document holds one thread, the app serves the chosen one. Do not name a variable step
Text never cuts: bubbles wrap, titles and the field ellipsize on one line. Keep time and status short; a long subtitle ("Assistant, a person replies within 2 hours") ellipsizes on a phone

components.name: checkbox
components.title: Checkbox
components.prompt: A "Remember me" checkbox that starts checked, and an unchecked newsletter opt-in.
teaches: Bind checked to a document variable ({"checked": "@remember"}) to preset or read it; omitted, the checkbox keeps its own state, starting unchecked
The whole row (box and label) is the touch target, at least 48 dp, and carries the label as its accessibility label; maxLines caps the label in a tight row

snippets.note: bound to @remember, which starts at 1 (checked)
no variable: it owns its state
the box and tick are a round rect and two lines

check.describe: Remember me shows a filled blue box with a white tick, the newsletter box is an empty outline; tapping a row flips it. Rows fill the width: at 195 dp the newsletter label wraps to two lines beside its box, at 450 dp nothing moves but the free space.

components.summary: A checkbox with its label: tapping the row flips its variable (0 or 1), then runs any extra `onClick` actions; the box fills and shows a tick when checked. A screen reader hears the label and the state, Checked or Not checked, which follows the value.
pitfalls: The tick is two drawLine calls, not an SVG path string: the Java JSON parser writes every path string padded to 1024 floats (about 4 KB)
The row is at least 48 dp (the touch minimum) and grows with its label, which takes the rest of the row and wraps, or ellipsizes at maxLines; the whole row (box and label) is the touch target
Checking animates at paint time: an animated local p = {"value": "@checked", "anim": 0.15} fades the fill and the tick in (paint alpha p); in mono they appear at once
`onClick` actions run after the flip: an app reading the exported `checked` on a hostNamedAction sees the new state

Accessibility: the row carries the label (contentDescription), the state (stateDescription) and the click, and a tappable row is one item, so the text inside is not read again. The state is cut from "Not checkedChecked    " by textSubtext at 11 * checked and trimmed, in the global section of a 0-size canvas placed before the row (the parsers bind the name in document order, and the row's modifiers come before its children). No role: the JSON semantics has no role key. About 140 B per call, and the named text ops keep it from compiling to a pattern

components.name: chip
components.title: Chip
components.prompt: A row of filter chips (Photography, Travel, Food) with Photography selected.
teaches: Call it with a label: {"Chip": {"label": "Travel"}}; a tap toggles its selected state
Bind selected to a document variable ("@photo", 1 to start selected) to preset or read it
Lay chips out in a row with spacedBy; they wrap their label

snippets.note: bound to @photo, which starts at 1 (selected)
the plain face: a pill on surfaceHigh
labelled from its label

check.describe: Photography is a blue pill with white text, Travel and Food are grey pills; tapping Travel selects it. The chips sit in a flow: at 234 dp Food wraps to a second line (140 dp tall to hold it), at 540 dp all three stay on one line.

components.summary: A pill-shaped filter chip: a tap toggles its 0/1 `selected` variable (then runs any extra `onClick` actions), and the selected face (filled with `color`) fades in over the plain one. A screen reader hears the label and Selected or Not selected, which follows the value; the 32 dp pill sits in a 48 dp tall touch target.
pitfalls: State colours without colour expressions: the two faces are stacked in one clipped box (same padding, same text, so the same size) and the top one's graphicsLayer alpha is the 0/1 state
Chips wrap their label: put them in a row (or several rows) with spacedBy; a `flow` ignores spacedBy
The label is one line with an ellipsis (maxLines 1): in a slot narrower than the label it ends in … instead of wrapping and being clipped by the pill
