Selecting cross-fades: the selected face's graphicsLayer alpha is the animated value {"value": "@selected", "anim": 0.2} (paint time; mono strips the motion)
`onClick` actions run after the toggle: an app reading the exported `selected` on a hostNamedAction sees the new state

Touch target: 8 dp of padding above and below the 32 dp pill make the chip 48 dp tall, all of it clickable; leave no extra vertical space between rows of chips (the padding is the gap). The width is the pill's: a label under about 20 dp ("On", one or two letters) leaves the target under 48 dp wide (no widthIn: the players disagree on it)

Accessibility: the chip carries the label (contentDescription), the state (stateDescription, Selected or Not selected) and the click. The state is cut from "Not selectedSelected    " by textSubtext at 12 * selected and trimmed, in the global section of a 0-size canvas placed before the chip, so it follows a bound variable at run time. About 150 B per call, and the named text ops keep it from compiling to a pattern

components.name: choice-chips
components.title: ChoiceChips
components.prompt: A tip percentage picked from labelled single-choice chips (10, 15, 20, 25 percent, no tip) and a segmented metric or imperial choice, with a line of text following both.
teaches: One call makes the whole group: {"ChoiceChips": {"label": "Tip", "items": ["10%", "15%"], "selected": "@tip"}}
selected is the index: read it from an expression or a TextChoice
style segmented reuses Tabs for two to four short items

snippets.note: single choice as wrapping pills, preset to the second item
the same call as a segmented track
each pill is announced with the group: Tip: 15%, Selected

check.describe: 15% and Metric are selected and the text reads Tip 15%, metric. Tapping 25% moves the fill, tapping 25% again keeps it, and the text follows. At 220 dp the pills wrap onto more lines; at 540 they stay on one.

components.summary: A labelled single choice: one short call makes a heading and a wrapping group of pills, a tap selects that item (a repeat tap keeps it, the others clear), and a screen reader hears the group with each item ("Tip: 15%", Selected). `selected` holds the 0-based index. style segmented uses Tabs' sliding pill instead of pills.
pitfalls: `selected` is the index, not a value: compute the value from it in the document ("10 + 5 * @tip"). A preset outside the list selects nothing until the next tap

In `onClick`, read @selected directly in the action's own expression. A variable derived from it in resources ("changed": "abs(@unit - @was)") still holds last frame's value during the tap, so it silently gives the old answer; CMP-25 hit this
Not for several independent on/off filters (use Chip) or a tab bar over panels (use Tabs). TextChoice only shows a word for an index: it takes no input, and pairs well with this for the result

Style chips wraps by itself (a `flow`): give it width and let its height grow; every line is 48 dp, all clickable, so don't put it in a box of fixed height. A label wider than the whole line ends in …
Style segmented is Tabs: it never wraps, and its tabs announce only their item ("Metric", Selected), after the heading in reading order. The chips style says the group in each item ("Tip: 15%")

Always expanded, never a pattern (its text and state ops): about 570 B per item and 850 B once per call (a three-item group is 2.6 KB alone, 1.8 KB as a second group in the same document; three plain Chips are 2.2 KB). A long list of choices belongs in a list, not pills
Mono: the selected pill is filled and the others are rings, so the state is a shape; no motion
`label` is required on purpose: without it a screen reader hears "10%" and no question

components.name: compactnumber
components.title: CompactNumber
components.prompt: Show a stock's volume, a balance and a market cap as short numbers: 38.4M, $1,234.50, $2.81T, correctly rounded, from live values.
teaches: Call {"CompactNumber": {"value": "@volume"}} for 38.4M; add prefix "$" or suffix " kWh"; it takes a live value
decimals keeps a price or balance in full ($1,234.50) below from, and short above it
It rounds before printing, moves to the next unit when rounding reaches 1000, and puts the sign before the currency: -$2.5M

snippets.note: a volume bound to a host value
a price with cents
see the call
see the call

check.describe: Volume 38.4M, Balance $1,234.50, Net -$2.5M, Price $0.00412, Energy 842 kWh, Market cap $2.81T, Saved $0.01, Steps 1,640. With the huge variables: 1M, $2.5M, -$0.4, $0.

components.summary: A number as one short text with K, M, B or T, an optional currency or unit, correctly rounded and signed: -$1.25M, 842K, 3.1 kWh, $0.0042. Takes a live value, sizes to its content, and is spoken in words ("$1.25 million").
pitfalls: Use this instead of writing K/M/B thresholds by hand. It rounds first (textFromFloat alone truncates the whole part: 102.9996 at 2 decimals prints 102.00), steps up a unit when rounding reaches 1000 (999,600 is 1M, not 1000K), and drops the sign when the rounded value is 0
Below 0.001 it prints 0: the format writes such small floats in E notation, so scale them yourself (price per 1000 units with a suffix)

For a price or a balance pass decimals (usually 2; 0 prints whole numbers with commas): $1,234.50 keeps its cents, 2.81B stays short. Without decimals, everything is three significant digits, so 102.99 prints 103 and 1640 prints 1.64K. Without decimals is right for volumes, counts, market caps
With decimals, a value under 0.1 prints by significant digits, right for a coin's unit price ($0.0042) and wrong for an amount ("$0.0116 saved"). For an amount add small: "fixed", which prints $0.01
A float holds about 7 digits: above 9,999,999 with decimals, the last digits are approximate, so leave from at 1,000,000 or lower

The prefix and suffix are text, so a host string works as a prefix through "@currency"; the spoken form is the shown form with the unit as a word: -$1.25M reads "-$1.25 million", which a screen reader says as minus. Say what it is in the caption beside it

Each call holds a 1 dp empty canvas, under the text in a box: text operations (the sign and the K/M/B cut from a string) only exist in a canvas. Its minus is a plain hyphen: the C++ player aborts when textSubtext cuts inside a multi-byte character. One call is about 900 B, so in a long list pass rounded numbers as host strings and use this for the headline figures

components.name: comparison
components.title: Comparison: options side by side on the same rows, a table when wide and two at a time on a phone
components.prompt: Compare three plans of a notes app (Free, Plus, Pro) on six features with prices and a Choose button, Plus marked most popular: a comparison table on a tablet or desktop, and on a phone two plans side by side that you can switch.
teaches: Give options (name, price, period, note, values per row) and rows; the component owns the table, the phone pair, the featured tint and badge, the selection ring and the host action
From labelMin + n x colMin + 32 dp a table with the header kept while rows scroll; narrower, two options side by side, each with a picker that steps to another option
Choose sets selected and sends hostNamedAction (action) with the index; values true and false draw a tick and a cross

snippets.note: the whole call: three plans on six rows
one option: its row values in order, true a tick, false a cross
every Choose sends choosePlan with the index
row labels; ticks and crosses are labelled Included and Not included

check.describe: Phone: Choose a plan, two cards (Plus with a Most popular badge, Pro), each a name picker, price, note and Choose; then six rows, each a caption and two values or ticks. Landscape 640x360 (short): a table, title in the corner, notes dropped. Tablet and desktop: a table centred, Plus column tinted with its badge, ticks and crosses aligned. chosen: Pro ringed with a filled Selected button. tap-picker: the right card steps from Pro to Free. desktop-tap: Pro chosen.

components.java_difference: one hostNamedAction name is sent by every Choose button (json2rc declares it once before the tree, the reference parser writes it into the first action list only: EXAMPLES_FINDINGS U58, Parser.ts EXTENSION); same length, different order
components.summary: A whole comparison screen from data: two to four options (plans, phones, laptops) on the same rows, each option a card with its name, price and a Choose button. From the width where every column fits (about 150 dp each, 440 to 760 dp wide) a real table: the options as columns beside a column of row labels, values aligned, the featured option tinted with a Most popular badge, the header kept while the rows scroll. Narrower, two options side by side on the same rows, each side with a picker that steps to another option; it opens on the featured one and its neighbour. Choose highlights the option with a ring and sends its index to the host.
pitfalls: The form follows the width, never the content: from labelMin + n x colMin + 32 dp (552 for 3 options, 692 for 4) a table with the options as columns; narrower, two options side by side with a picker on each. A 640 dp landscape phone gets the table for 3 options and the pair for 4

Why two at a time on a phone, not stacked cards: a comparison is read across a row (which plan has offline downloads?), and stacked cards make that a memory game; two columns of 160 dp on the same rows keep it a comparison. The pair opens on the featured option and its neighbour; each picker steps to the next option the other side is not showing

values are per option, in the order of rows, one for each row: true a tick, false a cross, null a dash, anything else a string. A number (2) is not text: write "2". A value is two lines at most (14 sp): about 16 characters a line in a 140 dp column

Every option is written three times (its table column and once on each side of the pair) and shown by visibility: the document grows with options x rows. Fine for 4 options and 15 rows; keep values short

One host action name (action, default choose) is sent by every Choose button with the index as a float: the converter declares the name once, the Java reference parser writes it into the first button's actions only (a known difference, see meta.java_difference). Read the index from the value, not from the name

Choose sets selected first, so the action carries the new index; Selected sends it again. -1 is nothing chosen yet. Bind selected to a resources variable to preset a choice (the ring and the filled button follow)

featured is static: a tint behind the column, a badge (featuredLabel, unless the option has its own badge) and the phone's starting pair. Use it for the recommended plan, not for the user's choice (that is selected)
Price and name are one line: keep prices short ("€9.99", "$1,199") and put the rest in period and note. The note is dropped when the window is under 480 dp tall, and so is the phone's title row
The header (cards with name, price and Choose) stays while the rows scroll. Heights are exact: 212 dp of header (176 when short), rowHeight per row; do not put it in a scrolling parent
width and height default to the window: pass them when it is not the whole window

components.name: coverart
components.title: Cover art
components.prompt: A designed placeholder for album art when the app has no image, which still reads on an always-on display.
teaches: A generated cover from theme colours only, turned by a seed
title gives the initial, symbol any icon; it fills its box or takes size

snippets.note: the call
the call
the call
the call

check.describe: Blue cover with a note, purple with M, green with a podcast symbol, each with discs and rings placed differently, and a wide blue poster strip. Mono: outlined squares with three rings and the symbol, visible on black and white.

components.summary: Album, podcast or video art that always looks designed: a generated cover from the theme (overlapping discs and rings, turned by a seed so covers differ, with a large symbol or the title's initial) that fills its box, with a slot on top for real art. In mono it is a ring cover, visible on black and on white.
pitfalls: It fills its box: inside a column or row, give the box a size or pass size. A canvas with nothing to measure against is 0 dp
The composition covers the box like an image (cropped to the long side); the symbol or initial stays centred at 45% of the short side
The initial is the first letter as the app sends it, not uppercased: send a capital. An empty host title shows the discs with nothing on them

Real images: pass "slots": {"image": [{"canvas": {"modifiers": ["fillMaxSize"], "commands": [{"type": "drawScaledBitmap", "image": "@cover", "srcLeft": 0, "srcTop": 0, "srcRight": 600, "srcBottom": 600, "dstLeft": 0, "dstTop": 0, "dstRight": "componentWidth()", "dstBottom": "componentHeight()", "scaleType": 5, "contentDescription": "Album cover"}]}}]}, with "cover": {"base64": "..."} or {"file": "cover.png"} under resources.bitmaps. PNG only; the image bytes go into the document, so keep it small. src is the image's own pixel size. scaleType 5 crops to fill. The slot's corners are rounded by CoverArt

components.name: dashboard-grid
components.title: DashboardGrid
components.prompt: Lay out a dashboard of different cards (KPIs, a chart, a ring, a ranked list) that is one scrolling column on a phone and two, three or four columns when wide, with a chart spanning two columns and cards in a row sharing a height.
teaches: Give the cards in reading order with a content node each and, where it matters, span (columns wanted), height (dp the content needs) and priority (column count from which it shows): the server packs every column count and the width picks one at run time

No holes: a card that does not fit the rest of a row moves down and the cards it leaves widen in proportion; every card of a row takes the row's height, and rows grow up to 1.3x to fill a taller window
Inside a card, "@cardWidth" and "@cardHeight" are the content box's size: cap a sparkline with min(@cardHeight - 80, 64) so a grown KPI card keeps a calm line

snippets.note: the cards, with a span-2 chart and a priority-2 list
more cards than a phone shows: the grid scrolls

check.describe: 360x640: Corner shop header, Revenue and Orders cards with a sparkline each, Sales by hour chart, Daily goal ring below (scrolls); the Top products card is hidden. 640x360: two KPI cards side by side, the chart full width under them. 800x1280: KPIs in a row, chart (2 columns) beside the goal ring, top products full width. 1280x800: KPIs and the chart in one row, goal and top products sharing the second row half and half.

components.summary: A whole dashboard screen from a list of cards: one column on a phone (stacked, scrolling), two on a landscape phone or small tablet, three or four when wide. Cards can span columns, cards in a row share a height, a row never has a hole (the cards of a short row widen in proportion to reach the edge) and rows grow to fill a tall window; low-priority cards show only when there is room. The column count and every span are packed on the server for each count and switched at run time by the width.
pitfalls: Content gets a box of exact width and height: a chart must fill it (fill: true, or fillMaxSize), and a component that needs its size given (RowList embedded, WorldMap) takes "@cardWidth" and "@cardHeight", which the grid replaces with that box's size. Nothing else in a card can read the grid's values

height is the content's height, title not included. Give each card what it needs at a phone's width: a row takes its tallest card and a 1-column phone gives each card exactly its own, so a KPI with height 120 beside a chart wastes nothing, but the same KPI alone on a phone is 120 dp tall
Do not put a StatTile or a Card in a card: they draw their own surface, so you get a tile inside a tile. Use BigNumber (and a Sparkline or TrendSparkline under it) for a KPI card

Order is reading order at every width: the grid does not reorder. Put the cards that should share a row next to each other (two KPIs, then a span-2 chart) and a span-2 chart after an even number of single cards, or its row-mate stretches to fill the hole it leaves

span is clamped to the columns there are, so a span-3 card is full width on 1 and 2 columns. A card that does not fit what is left of a row moves to the next row and the cards it leaves widen in proportion to their spans (two single cards in 3 columns get 1.5 each): no holes, but their edges no longer line up with the columns of other rows
priority 2 hides a card below 2 columns (a phone); it is still in the document. Keep at least one card at priority 1, and never hide the only place a number is shown

Rows grow up to grow times (1.3) to fill a taller window: content that fills (charts, rings) uses it, fixed content keeps its size and sits at align. A window much taller than the content still has space under the grid; set grow higher or add cards
Text does not shrink: the grid scrolls when there is not room, which is what a phone does; a widget-size window should not use it

components.name: date-label
components.title: Date label
components.prompt: Show today's date as text in several formats: a long one with the weekday and month names, a short one, and ISO and numeric day/month/year forms.
teaches: {"DateLabel": {}} shows "Thu 29 Oct" from the host clock; format picks medium (29 Oct 2026), long (Thursday, 29 October 2026), iso, dmy or mdy

Weekday and month names are cut from one constant string with textSubtext at (weekDay() - 1) × width, which the Java parser converts (textLookup over a data list does not, U4); full names are padded to 9 characters and trimmed
The parts are joined with textMerge into one string and drawn with drawTextAnchored, so align start, center or end places the whole date in the width the label fills
A date wider than its label is measured with textMeasure and drawn under one scale of min(1, componentWidth() / width), so it shrinks instead of being cut off

A screen reader hears the full date ("Thursday 29 October" for the short label): an empty box over the canvas carries a contentDescription of a text variable built in the canvas, after it, since "@name" resolves only once the name is defined

snippets.note: the long format, with full weekday and month names
the short format: 3-letter names cut with textSubtext
ISO 8601, zero-padded with textFromFloat flags 12
align: end, drawn at componentWidth() with panX 1

check.describe: On Thursday 29 October 2026 the labels read "Thursday, 29 October 2026", "Thu 29 Oct" (centred), "29 Oct 2026", "2026-10-29" (blue), "29/10/2026" and "10/29/2026" (end-aligned). On Sunday 3 January 2027 (the january render) the names change to "Sunday, 3 January 2027" and "Sun 3 Jan". Each label fills the column's width: at 200 dp the 18 dp long date is wider than the column and is scaled down to fit on its line; at 420 dp the centred and end-aligned ones follow the width. A screen reader announces each date in words with full names: "Thursday, 29 October 2026", "Thursday 29 October", "29 October 2026" (medium, iso, dmy) and "October 29, 2026" (mdy).

components.summary: Today's date from the host clock, drawn as one line that fills its width, in a static format: "Thu 29 Oct", "29 Oct 2026", "Thursday, 29 October 2026", 2026-10-29, 29/10/2026 or 10/29/2026.
pitfalls: A date wider than the label is scaled down to fit (textMeasure, then one scale about the anchor), never cut off or wrapped

A screen reader hears the date in words, not the drawn text: the canvas has no semantics, and an empty box over it (same size) carries a contentDescription of a text variable built in the canvas (full weekday and month names, the day without a pad). It sits after the canvas because the parser resolves "@name" only once the name is defined: on the canvas's own modifiers it would be the literal text

The date is drawn on a canvas that fills its parent's width (fillMaxWidth, 1.4 × fontSize tall): in a row, put it in a weighted box, or it has no width. It is drawn because the Java parser accepts textSubtext and textTransform only among canvas commands, not in a layout text, and the names need them
weekDay() is 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday) and calendarMonth() 1 to 12: subtract 1 before indexing

Names come from one constant string cut with textSubtext at (field - 1) × width: every name is padded to 9 characters; the full name is it trimmed (textTransform operation 3), the 3-letter one its first 3 characters (a second textSubtext). textLookup over an addDataList would be shorter to write, but the Java parser drops the list's id (U4), so the document would only convert with json2rc
The names are English; for another language, copy the component and change the two name strings and the spoken order (keep every name the same width)

Each call writes its name texts under fixed names (dateLabelDay, dateLabelMonth, dateLabelText, dateLabelSpoken): a later DateLabel redefines them after an earlier one has used them, which is fine, but don't read them from outside the component
The date changes at midnight with no repaint of its own: a document that shows only a date is redrawn when the host redraws it

components.name: delta
components.title: Delta
components.prompt: Show a change as an arrow and signed number, green or red, that still reads in mono and to a screen reader, such as +2.40% and +$3.18 (+2.40%).
teaches: Call {"Delta": {"value": "@chg"}}: the sign chooses arrow, sign and colour, after rounding, so a tiny change is flat
amount shows both: +$3.18 (+2.40%). Use style pill in lists
suffix and spoken change the unit, invert makes a fall good
A screen reader hears "up 2.40 percent", once

snippets.note: spoken as up 2.40 percent
amount and percent
see the call
see the call

check.describe: Green up arrows and +2.40%, a solid pill, +$3.18 (+2.40%), a green down arrow with −4 min, and a grey dash with 0.00%. In mono the arrows and signs stay. With down: red −1.26%, −$2.50 (−1.26%), red +3 min.

components.summary: A change as an arrow, a sign and a number, green for up and red for down (or the reverse with invert), that still reads in mono by its arrow and sign and is spoken as words: "up 2.40 percent". Text or solid pill; optionally an amount and a percent together, +$2.40 (+1.25%).
pitfalls: The number is rounded before printing and the direction is taken after rounding, so 0.004% is flat and shows 0.00%, not a green arrow on zero
Three copies of the row (up, down, flat) are switched with visibility, because a text's colour can't be an expression. So one call costs about 1 KB: cheap for a screen, count it for long lists

Say what the change is relative to in the words beside it ("today", "since open"): nothing here knows the period. A signed value like -0.4 with suffix " min" gives −0.40 min: set decimals 0 for whole units
Colour is decided from `value`, not from whether the number is good: pass invert for costs
Prefix goes after the sign: −$2.40

components.name: digital-clock
components.title: Digital clock
components.prompt: Show the current time as a digital clock, HH:MM:SS in 24-hour format, and a smaller 12-hour one.
teaches: {"DigitalClock": {}} shows HH:MM from the host clock; showSeconds: true adds :SS and repaints every second
format: "12h" gives 1..12 hours followed by a smaller AM/PM (showAmPm: false hides it); fontSize sizes every field
use24h: "@use24h" follows the device's 12/24-hour preference, which the app must send: both hour texts are written and an integer visibility shows one

snippets.note: 24-hour with seconds
12-hour at 28 sp

check.describe: At 22:10:05 the first clock reads 22:10:05 and the second 10:10 followed by a small PM, colons in blue. The clock is as wide as its digits (about 155 dp at 40 sp with seconds): at 200 dp it still fits, at 390 dp it stays at the start. It does not shrink: below about 190 dp pick a smaller fontSize.

components.summary: HH:MM or HH:MM:SS from the host clock, in 24-hour or 12-hour format (with AM/PM), fixed or chosen at run time by a host variable, with zero-padded fields.
pitfalls: flags 12 (PAD_PRE_ZERO) makes 9 print as 09; flags 4 (PAD_PRE_NONE) drops the pad, for a 12-hour hour
12-hour hour: (floor(timeInHr()) + 11) % 12 + 1 gives 1..12 (12 at 00:xx and 12:xx); PM is floor(timeInHr() / 12) = 1, so 00:05 is 12:05 AM, 11:59 AM, 12:00 PM and 23:59 11:59 PM

The device's 12/24-hour preference is not visible to a document: the app must send it, as the variable passed to use24h. Both hour texts are then in the document, one GONE, and the AM/PM marker is hidden in 24-hour mode
Each field is its own text in a row, so a proportional font makes the clock's width change as digits change; give the row a fixed width if it must not move
AM and PM are two texts, one GONE (an integer visibility from floor(timeInHr() / 12)); the marker is centred on the digits' row, not on their baseline

components.name: divider
components.title: Divider
components.prompt: Thin separator lines between the rows of a settings list, one full width and one inset.
teaches: {"Divider": {}} is a 1 dp rule across its parent; put it between rows of a column
inset indents it from the start to line up with the row text: 56 after a 24 dp icon (16 + 24 + 16), 72 after a 40 dp avatar

snippets.note: the default, full width
inset 56 to line up with the text after the icons

check.describe: Three rows on a rounded surface; the rule under Wi-Fi spans the card, the one under Bluetooth starts under the text, 56 dp in. Both rules fill the card's width at 195 and 450 dp; the inset one keeps its 56 dp start.

components.summary: A 1 dp horizontal rule across its parent, optionally inset from the start to line up with list text.
pitfalls: The inset is padding on an outer box around a filled inner box: padding before a background on the same box insets the background in Java and the TypeScript player but not in the C++ player, so the two-box form is the one that looks the same everywhere

components.name: donut-chart
components.title: DonutChart
components.prompt: Show weekly visits as a donut chart with the total in the middle, next to a donut of traffic sources.
teaches: Call {"DonutChart": {"values": "@visits", "label": "visits"}} with the name of a float array in resources.floatArrays; export it and the host can replace the data
Each slice is its value's share of the sum, clockwise from 12 o'clock; the sum is printed in the centre (showTotal) above the label
fill: true in a sized or weighted parent scales the ring to fit, centred

snippets.note: bound to the exported float array visits
one drawArc per value, in a loop over the array
three slices, thinner ring, secondary colour
the loop rotates the canvas by each slice's angle, so the next starts where it ended

check.describe: Left: a blue ring of eight slices, solid to pale clockwise from 12 o'clock, 490 visits in the centre; right: a violet ring of three slices (58, 27, 15) with 100 sources %. With variables {visits: [10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 90]} the last slice takes more than half the ring and the total reads 160. At 234 and 540 dp wide the rings shrink to share the row, or stay at the row's height, centred.

components.summary: A donut (ring) chart of a float array: one slice per value, clockwise from 12 o'clock, each value's share of the total, in tones of one colour separated by 2 dp gaps, with the total and a caption in the centre.
pitfalls: values is the name of a float array ("@visits" declared in resources.floatArrays), not a JSON list: one loop draws every slice, so a host that sets the exported array redraws the ring, whatever its length

There is no running sum in an expression, so each slice starts at 12 o'clock and the loop rotates the canvas by that slice's angle after drawing it: the rotations accumulate across iterations, inside one save
Slices are told apart by a 2 dp gap and by tone (paint alpha falls with the index), not by a palette: the library has no categorical colours. In mono there is no tone: slices alternate thick and thin

A fixed `size` is the box the call asks for; where the space varies, pass fill: true in a sized or weighted parent. Either way the ring is drawn at `size` and a canvas variable (min(componentWidth(), componentHeight())) with one translate + scale fits it to the box it got, centred, so a call clamped by a smaller parent shrinks instead of being cut off, and stroke widths scale with it. Every coordinate stays a folded number

components.name: equalizer
components.title: Equalizer
components.prompt: A small now playing indicator with bars that dance while the music plays.
teaches: An eased value whose target ticks only while playing: bars move, then the document goes idle when paused
Mono draws a still picture

snippets.note: the call
the call
the call
the call

check.describe: Three indicators: large bars at varied heights, four short grey bars at rest, small bars. Mono: fixed bars, not moving.

components.summary: A small "now playing" indicator: four rounded bars that dance while playing and rest low when paused. It repaints only while playing, and is a still, distinct picture in mono looks.
pitfalls: Bars keep moving only while playing is 1: the eased value that drives them stops, so a paused document goes idle. While playing, the document repaints every frame
In mono it does not move: a fixed set of bars when playing, four short ones when paused

components.name: expandable-row
components.title: ExpandableRow
components.prompt: Make a list of rows where tapping a row opens its details under it and tapping again closes it, with only one row open at a time.
teaches: Call {"ExpandableRow": {"title": ..., "slots": {"details": [...]}}}: the whole row is the tap target, it opens on a tap and closes on the next, and the details take no space until it opens
One open at a time: bind the same variable on every row ("selected": "@open") and number them ("index": 1, 2, 3). Tapping the open row sets it to 0
Put a badge or an icon in slots.leading and a value in slots.trailing; the title takes the remaining width and ellipsizes, or takes two lines with titleLines 2

snippets.note: a row with leading, trailing and details slots, bound to the group's variable
titleLines 2: a long title wraps in the weighted column and the row grows
tapping sets open to 3, or to 0 when it is already open
a row keeping its own state, with an accessibility label of its own

check.describe: Four rows; Storage is open with its progress bar under it and an up chevron, the others are closed with down chevrons and take only their header. The 'closed' render taps Storage so it closes. Resized, the rows fill the width: at 200 the titles ellipsize while slots and chevrons keep their size.

components.summary: A full-width row the user taps to open and close: optional leading and trailing slots, a weighted one-line title with an optional subtitle, a chevron that follows the state, and a details slot that takes no space until open. Rows sharing a `selected` variable open one at a time.
pitfalls: Group rows by binding the same variable and numbering them from 1: {"selected": "@open", "index": 2}. Tapping the open row sets the variable to 0, so 0 must stay free. Left unbound, each row keeps its own state and several can be open

The row has no fixed height: it grows with its content and with the details, so whatever holds it must have room for it open. In a short box, hide other rows while one is open (visible, or a visibility around it) or put the rows in a verticalScroll

titleLines 2 wraps at spaces only. In the C++ render a single word wider than the column loses its end on the first line with no ellipsis, so if a host may send long single words (place names) keep one line, which ellipsizes cleanly, or use stack to give the title the full width

The row is tappable, so a screen reader treats it as one item: the player merges the texts inside it (click modifiers are MERGE mode) and announces `label` and the state. So `label` must say everything, including what the details show when open. Build it live with textMerge from the same variables the row shows
Padding and spacedBy take literals only, so verticalPadding is written as two spacer boxes; minHeight is a heightIn minimum and does accept an expression
Below 48 dp (compact, or a small minHeight) the row misses the touch-target guideline; the audit reports it as info. Keep the default wherever three rows fit

Costs about 700 B per extra row before its slots, always expanded: the body declares a named text for the state, so it cannot be a definePattern template. Use one component call per row, not a stateLayout of copies

components.name: flow-diagram
components.title: FlowDiagram
components.prompt: Show an article's publishing workflow: draft, editor review, legal check, publish, with a 'changes' loop back to draft; the app says which step the article is at.
teaches: Call {"FlowDiagram": {"nodes": [...], "edges": ["a > b", ["b", "a", "changes"]]}}: the server places the steps in layers and routes the arrows
current: "@currentStep" (a host variable, never named step) makes the statuses follow the app: steps it can be reached from show done, it shows active, the rest pending
status ok/active/failed/pending marks each step by shape and colour; an arrow back up is a loop
It runs top to bottom when tall, left to right when wide, and shows a step summary when tiny

snippets.note: the call: steps as boxes, arrows in one canvas
diagram or step summary by visibility, from the size
each step's label and status is read
current: @currentStep

check.describe: Four steps down the screen: Draft ticked (done), Editor review filled (current 1), Legal check and Publish pending; approved beside the arrow to Legal check, a changes arrow back up to Draft. legal: Draft and Editor review ticked, Legal check filled. Wide: left to right. 160: Step 2 of 4.

currentStep.meaning: 0-based index of the current step in nodes; -1 not started, 4 all done

components.summary: A process or flow diagram laid out by the server: name the steps (with a status) and the arrows between them (with an optional label), and it places them in layers with few crossings, routes the arrows at right angles, runs top to bottom on a tall screen and left to right on a wide one, and shows the current step and a dot per step when the space is too small.
pitfalls: Leave width and height out: it fills the window and adapts (orientation, scale, summary). Under a title or inside padding pass what is left as an expression ("windowHeight() - 64"); numbers are only upper bounds, so a size written for one screen still fits a smaller one
Leave direction auto unless the shape of the screen is known; right and down are only preferences, right! and down! pin it and can leave too little room
Labels wrap to two lines (three when every label is long and the flow is short) and then end in an ellipsis: keep step names under about 30 characters
Edge labels sit beside the arrow just after its start: one or two words. Two labelled arrows leaving one step go out of separate ports so their labels part
A process deeper than about 7 steps does not fit a landscape phone: it shows the summary there. Pin direction only if you know the shape of the screen
Each node is a text box (measured, checked), arrows are one canvas: about 200 B per step and 100 B per arrow

current reads an index into nodes: a host variable declared in resources (e.g. {"variables": {"currentStep": {"value": 1, "export": true}}}) and passed as "@currentStep" (never name it step: that hides the step() function). Each step that follows it costs three faces, about 3x a static step

components.name: fretboard
components.title: Fretboard
components.prompt: Show guitar chord diagrams: A7 in open position, B minor as a barre chord with its intervals under the strings, and the shape x-x-7-9-8-9 named for me.
teaches: {"Fretboard": {"chord": "Bm"}}: the server finds a playable shape (x24432, barre at 2) and its fingers
{"frets": "x-x-7-9-8-9"}: a fingering is read low string first, its chord named (A7) and its position shown (7fr)
The diagram is literal geometry in a 100-wide box scaled uniformly to the canvas: no expression per string or dot

snippets.note: a chord name, voiced by the server
barre and intervals; one uniform scale
a fingering; the description names every string

check.describe: Three chord diagrams with titles: A7 (x02020, open and muted markers, fingers 1 and 2, notes A E G C♯ E), Bm (barre at fret 2 with finger 1, fingers 2 3 4, intervals R 5 R ♭3 5), A7 at 7fr (x-x-7-9-8-9).

components.summary: A guitar chord diagram: strings, frets, finger dots with numbers, open and muted strings, a barre, the position (5fr) and the notes under the strings, from a chord name ("Dm": the server finds a playable shape) or a fingering ("xx0231").
pitfalls: Give the chord name or the fingering, never draw dots yourself; the fingering is low string first (the way chord charts read left to right)
From a name the server picks one shape (open position first, then the lowest barre shape): give frets for a particular voicing

Fingers are worked out when not given: one finger per fret from the lowest, a barre with finger 1 when the lowest fret holds several strings and five or more notes need fingers; give fingers to show your own
The diagram keeps its proportions: inside a smaller box it shrinks, centred, with every label

components.name: gallery-grid
components.title: GalleryGrid: a grid of pictures whose columns follow the width
components.prompt: Make a game library: each game a cover with its name and genre, in sections, two columns on a phone and more on a tablet; tapping a game launches it.
teaches: Give items as objects: {"title", "caption", "meta", "art" or "symbol" and "color", "badge", "section"}. The component owns the header, the column count, the tile size, the aspect ratio, the scrolling and the selection
Columns follow the width: 2 at 360 dp, 3 at 640, 4 at 800, 6 at 1280 with the default minTile 150; the cover keeps aspect (here 1.25, portrait) at every size
A tap sets selected (ringed in primary) and then runs onClick, which reads the new index: one hostNamedAction launch with the game's number

snippets.note: the whole call: ten games in two sections
the tapped game's index goes to the app
a tile with a section heading before it and a badge on its cover; read as title and caption
the grid scrolls under the header when the tiles do not fit

check.describe: Phone (360x640): Library, 10 games installed, then Continue playing and two columns of portrait covers (Tidewater, Cog & Lever, Night Circuit with percentages), Installed below. 640x360: three columns. 800x1280: four columns, all ten games. 1280x800: six columns. tap: Cog & Lever ringed in primary. Mono: ring covers, white on black and black on white.

components.java_difference: one hostNamedAction name (launch) used by every tile: json2rc declares it once before the tree on purpose (Parser.ts EXTENSION, EXAMPLES_FINDINGS U58); the reference writes it inside the first tile's action list only, so the other tiles would send a nameless action until the first was tapped
components.summary: A whole gallery screen from data: an optional header, then a scrolling grid of visual items (a picture or drawn tile, a title, a caption and a price or count), with optional section headings. The column count follows the width (2 on a phone, 3 on a landscape phone, 4 on a portrait tablet, up to 6 on a wide window, more when the window is short so a whole tile fits), every tile keeps its picture's aspect ratio, and a tap sets the selected index (ringed) and runs onClick.
pitfalls: Columns follow the window, never the content: floor((width - 2 * (16 - gap / 2)) / (minTile + gap)), raised when the window is short so a whole tile (picture and text) takes at most 85% of the grid's height, kept between minColumns and maxColumns. With the defaults (minTile 150, gap 12, square): 2 at 360x640, 3 at 640x360, 4 at 800x1280, 6 at 1280x800; a portrait aspect (1.25) gets 4 at 640x360

Every tile keeps aspect (picture height over width) at every column count; only the text under it is fixed (title one line, caption and meta one line). Keep meta short ("$24", "4.8"): it is never cut, the caption is ellipsized beside it

art fills the picture box exactly: a canvas or box with fillMaxSize (draw from componentWidth() and componentHeight(), not from a size), or CoverArt with no size. In plain style the box clips art to radius; in card style the card clips it
A section field starts a full-width heading before its tile and a new row of tiles; a row before it may stay short. There is no sticky header
The grid scrolls inside height minus the header: no weights or fillMaxHeight inside art. Every tile is written into the document: fine for tens of items; for hundreds, page them from the app

Tap sets selected (from 0, -1 none) and then runs onClick, which sees the new index: send it with {"type": "hostNamedAction", "name": "open", "value": "@sel", "valueType": "float", "actionType": 0}. The action is written in every tile, so the name is used many times: json2rc declares it once on purpose (the reference parser writes it only in the first tile's list, so its bytes differ)

Each distinct symbol in a generated cover is a Material Symbols path written once, about 1.5 KB: twelve different symbols are most of a 38 KB document (CMP-46). Reuse symbols, or pass art drawn from a few primitives (CMP-45's Snapshot is about 0.5 KB a photo)
Not for tiles of different kinds (a chart beside a list beside a gauge): that is a dashboard grid. Not for rows of data that become tiles when wide: that is RowList. GalleryGrid is pictures first
width and height default to the window: pass them when it sits under a bar or inside a pane (a NavShell page: give height the page's height and set NavShell scroll to false)

components.name: gauge
components.title: Gauge
components.prompt: A dial gauge for CPU usage that turns amber then red as it climbs.
teaches: Call it with a value and a label: {"Gauge": {"value": "@cpu", "label": "CPU %"}}; the label is also the accessibility label
min and max set the range (0..100); warnAt and alertAt are fractions of it where amber and red start
A literal value folds to fixed arcs; a "@variable" keeps them live
bandLo and bandHi (value units) mark an ideal band on the track: green inside it, amber below or above, with shape (a filled or hollow dot) carrying the state in mono

snippets.note: bound to the exported @cpu
a literal value past alertAt: red
zone colour follows the value

check.describe: Left: a green arc at 42 labelled CPU %; right: a red arc at 91 labelled Temp °C. variables {cpu: 75} turns the left one amber. Called with fill: true in two weighted halves, the gauges scale with the space: at 234 dp wide they shrink to fit side by side, at 540 dp they are centred in their halves at the row's height.

components.summary: A 240° dial gauge: a value arc from min to max, green, then amber past warnAt and red past alertAt, with the value and a label in the centre. Or, with bandLo and bandHi, an ideal band (soil moisture 40-70 %) marked on the track: the value is green inside it and amber below or above it.
pitfalls: Zone colours without colour expressions: three arcs of the same sweep are drawn on top of each other, green always, amber with paint alpha step(f, warnAt), red with alpha step(f, alertAt); the topmost visible one wins. The text paint then resets alpha to 1
step(x, edge) is x > edge, and clamp takes (min, max, value)
The fraction and the sweep are locals: each is one float expression shared by the three arcs and both alphas (a literal value folds them to numbers, so nothing is computed at run time)

A fixed `size` is the box the call asks for: a 160 dp gauge still overflows a narrower widget. Where the space varies, pass fill: true and give the call a sized or weighted parent (weights ignore spacedBy: put the gap in a padding). Either way the face is drawn at `size` and a canvas variable (min(componentWidth(), componentHeight())) with one translate + scale fits it to the box it got, centred, so a call clamped by a smaller parent shrinks instead of being cut off; every coordinate stays a folded number. The variable keeps the call out of pattern mode, where min() over componentWidth()/componentHeight() comes out wrong (C++ and TS players)

An ideal band (bandLo..bandHi) replaces the zones: the track gets a wider translucent success segment with a tick at each end, and the value arc is amber with a success copy on top at paint alpha inBand = (1 - step(bandLo, value)) * (1 - step(value, bandHi)), ends inclusive. In mono the band is a thicker grey track section between two ticks, and a dot rides the end of the value arc: filled inside the band, hollow (background-filled ring) outside. The band is on when bandHi is given: pass both, and don't write a literal bandHi of 0 (it reads as absent; use a variable or a tiny offset)

components.name: goal-bar
components.title: GoalBar
components.prompt: Show steps and water against daily goals as bars with a goal mark, and what happens past the goal.
teaches: {"GoalBar": {"value": "@steps", "target": 10000, "label": "Steps"}} fills its parent's width
The tick stays visible with room beyond it; past the goal the bar rescales and +N appears

snippets.note: line, bar and tick on one canvas
spoken as one sentence
every length and sweep is an expression of the value and the box
numbers are rounded, formatted and fitted

check.describe: Steps at 84% of the way to a tick at 80% of the track; Water past its tick with +600 in green; Workout empty.

components.summary: A labelled bar against a goal: the label, value / goal and the amount past it on one baseline, over a tinted track with a tick at the goal and room beyond it, so reaching and passing the goal are both visible. For steps, water, protein, savings. Read as one sentence.
pitfalls: It fills its parent's width: in a row, give it a weighted box. Its height is fixed by textSize and height
Unlike ProgressBar, the goal is always marked: the track runs on past it (goalAt), so a full bar never reads as a limit. Use ProgressBar when the end of the bar is the limit
The line scales down together when it would not fit the width, so label and numbers never touch
Drawn text does not follow the system font scale

components.name: icon
components.title: Icon
components.prompt: Show a status bar with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, battery, notifications and settings icons, the home icon in each style and filled, and a filled heart for a liked state.
teaches: {"Icon": {"name": "wifi"}} draws a Material Symbols icon at 24 dp in onSurface; style (outlined, rounded, sharp), filled, size and color change it
Each icon's path is written once in resources.paths and shared by every call of it
Give a label when the icon carries meaning on its own; a filled variant marks a selected or active state

snippets.note: a status row: labelled icons, one tinted primary
the same icon in the three styles and filled
a status icon with its accessibility label

check.describe: A status row (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, a battery at five bars, then a primary bell and a gear at the right), a row of four 36 dp home icons captioned outlined, rounded, sharp and filled (the filled one primary), and a filled red heart before a line of text. Light and dark follow the theme; mono draws every icon in the mono foreground. At 280 dp the rows tighten, at 480 they spread.

components.summary: A Material Symbols icon (4,157 icons, outlined, rounded or sharp, plain or filled) drawn as a vector path, tinted with one colour. Use it for every symbol on screen instead of a text glyph or emoji.
pitfalls: Icons replace text glyphs and emoji (◐ ★ ☀ ✓): those render differently per font, can't take theme colours and are usually only approximations
The name must exist: an unknown name fails with the closest matches; search by meaning with find kind "icons" (tags such as 'battery', 'signal', 'weather')
Each icon's path is stored once per document however many times it is called; different icons each add about 0.5 to 2 KB
autoMirrored icons (arrows, back) are not flipped for right-to-left layouts

components.name: icon-button
components.title: IconButton
components.prompt: A toolbar of round icon buttons: menu, a filled add button that counts taps, outlined search, a close button that resets the count, and a disabled one.
teaches: The icon goes in slots.icon (about 24 dp); the button draws only the round face, filled or ringed, and the press ripple
label is the accessibility label: an icon button has no visible text, so say what it does
enabled: false dims the icon, drops the click and announces it as disabled; a runtime 0/1 value ("@canSend") makes it follow the host while it plays

snippets.note: filled: each tap adds one to @added
standard: the icon alone, labelled Menu
outlined: a ring of two stacked backgrounds

check.describe: Five 40 dp round buttons in a row: a menu icon, a blue disc with a white plus, a blue ring with a magnifier, a close cross and a grey disabled disc; tapping the plus adds one to the count below it, the cross sets it back to 0. The row keeps its size when resized: at 260 dp it still fits, at 450 dp the free space is at the end.

components.summary: A round button holding only an icon (40 dp, or `size`): standard (icon alone), filled or outlined, in a touch target of at least 48 dp. Labelled for accessibility from its label; enabled (true/false, or a 0/1 variable or expression read at run time) dims it and drops the click.
pitfalls: The icon is the caller's: draw it in a colour that reads on the face (onPrimary on a filled button, which is black in mono and white otherwise; onSurface or the button colour on the others)

The face is `size` dp (40) round and the touch target at least 48 dp: below 48 the face sits in transparent padding of (48 - size) / 2 (4 dp at 40) that is part of the click, so neighbours can sit with no spacedBy and still show a gap of 8 dp
The outlined ring is two stacked backgrounds, not a border (border can't take a theme colour): set surface to whatever the button sits on, or the inside shows the background colour

In mono a disabled filled button is a grey disc with the icon undimmed: the onPrimary icon reads on it (black on grey, white on dark grey). A ring would show an onPrimary icon on the surface colour, where it vanishes. Every other face keeps its shape. So a filled button's icon must be onPrimary even when disabled: an icon drawn in onDisabled is grey on the grey disc in mono
Press feedback is the onClick ripple Java draws on every click (no ripple modifier, or Java draws two); it is clipped to the round face

A runtime enabled ("@var" or an expression, exactly 0 or 1, reading resources variables only) stacks a disabled face, an enabled face and the icon: the faces are switched by visibility and only the enabled one has the onClick, so at 0 a tap does nothing. The icon slot is written once, above the faces, dimmed by the state, so it costs about 250 B more than a literal, not a second icon. The icon is therefore outside the click: label the button, not the icon, or a screen reader reads the icon's label as a second item

`size` scales the icon slot with a graphicsLayer (size / 40, about the centre, at paint time): draw the icon at 24 dp as for a 40 dp button. Its layout size stays 24 dp, so a size under 24 is not a good idea. At 48 or more the button writes a padding of 0

components.name: inputs-result
components.title: InputsResult
components.prompt: A coffee order: the result stays visible above a size choice and a stepper, stacked on a phone and side by side when wide.
teaches: Give it the result and the inputs as slots, and the one number it can't measure: resultHeight
Use it as the document's root

snippets.note: the whole screen in one call
the inputs scroll in the space the result leaves

check.describe: The result card is on top with the inputs below it; at 600x300 it sits to their left; at 240x200 the card is whole and the inputs scroll under it.

components.summary: A whole-screen template for a calculator or form with a live answer: the result stays on screen and the inputs scroll in the space left. Stacked (result on top) when narrow, side by side (result on the left) from sideAt. Decided by window width, never by content.
pitfalls: Use it as the document's root: it fills the window, paints the background and pads itself, and its sizes come from the window. Inside something smaller it is wrong; there use AdaptiveSplit with your own width and height

resultHeight is a number you must get right: the format has no way to size the inputs from a measured result, and too small clips the result (text cut this way gives a text_overflow warning; anything drawn gets no finding). Sum it (Card padding 32 + 2 plus the content) and look at the smallest size
The inputs scroll, so nothing in them should be weighted or fill the height, and no onRelease control (a Slider's) inside a scroll: it fires for the last one wherever the finger was
Result first is deliberate: above the hand when stacked, and on tall windows the empty space is at the bottom, not between input and answer. Reading order is result, then inputs
Always expanded (it calls AdaptiveSplit and declares a scroll), one call per document: the cost is once, about 700 B over a bare column

components.name: key-value-row
components.title: KeyValueRow
components.prompt: List a few device details as label / value lines, with the value right-aligned, and a toggle on the last line.
teaches: Call {"KeyValueRow": {"key": "Storage", "value": "64 GB"}}: the muted key on the left, the value pushed to the right end
Pass a text expression as value for a live number: {"type": "textFromFloat", "value": "@photos", "whole": 6, "decimal": 0, "flags": 5}
Leave value out and fill slots.trailing with a control (a Switch here) for a settings line

snippets.note: a fixed key and value
a live value from the exported variable photos, pushed right by the row's weighted spacer
no value, a Switch in the trailing slot

check.describe: A rounded card with three lines: Storage 64 GB, Photos 1284 (right-aligned) and Cloud backup with its switch on; setting photos to 7 shows 7. At 160 dp the keys end in … while the values and the switch keep their size; at 540 dp the values move to the end.

components.summary: A property line: a muted key on the left, its value pushed to the right end, with an optional trailing slot (a Switch, a chevron).
pitfalls: The key sits in the weighted box (weight 1; the text is one line with an ellipsis): it takes what the value and the trailing slot leave and shortens with … in a narrow row, instead of pushing them out; the box's end padding is the gap. Weight the box, not the text: the C++ player gives a weighted text its full width and squeezes the siblings after it to nothing. No spacedBy in a row holding a weight: weights ignore spacedBy, so the row overflows by the gaps (Java does this too). Fixed spacer boxes instead
A live number needs textFromFloat with enough `whole` digits (whole is the count of integer digits kept: whole 1 prints 12 as 2) and flags 5 (no padding)

components.name: label-value
components.title: LabelValue
components.prompt: Show a boarding pass strip: gate, seat and boarding time as small labels over large values, then flight, status and bag-drop rows, each pair read by a screen reader as one item ("Gate, B34").
teaches: Call {"LabelValue": {"label": "Gate", "value": "@gate"}}: a screen reader hears one item, "Gate, B34", not the label and the value separately
The two texts are drawn on one canvas whose semantics is textMerge("Gate, ", value): JSON semantics has no merge mode, so two layout texts under a described container are read three times
layout inline puts the pair on one line; align spread pushes the value to the end, start, center or end place the pair as a group
A line wider than its box is measured with textMeasure and scaled down about its anchor; in a row, give each LabelValue a weighted box

snippets.note: read as "Gate, B34"; the value is a string variable the host sets
align center, with a description that spells the seat
inline spread: the label at the start, the value at the end
inline, large, at the end: the group shrinks together when it is too wide

check.describe: A row of three stacked pairs, Gate B34, Seat 14C (centred) and Boards 09:40 (blue, at the end), with small muted labels over 28 dp values; then Terminal 2E, Hall L (small), Flight … AF 1234 across the width, Status Delayed 25 min in red and Bag drop closes 08:55 at the end. The accessibility tree has exactly one node per pair: "Gate, B34", "Seat, 14 C", "Boards, 09:40", "Terminal, 2E, Hall L", "Flight, AF 1234", "Status, Delayed 25 min", "Bag drop closes, 08:55". At 220 dp the large values shrink to fit their thirds; at 480 dp the pairs follow the width.

components.summary: A label and its value (Gate / B34, Seat / 14C, Balance / €1,240) read by a screen reader as ONE item, "Gate, B34": the label small and muted over the value (stacked) or beside it (inline), drawn on one canvas that carries the merged description, so the two texts are never read separately. Lines too wide for the box shrink to fit.
pitfalls: One accessibility node: the label and the value are drawn on one canvas (drawTextAnchored), and the canvas's semantics carries textMerge("<label>, ", value). Two layout texts under a container with a contentDescription are read three times (the container, then each text): the JSON semantics has no merge mode (the parsers always write SET), so drawing is the only way to keep the parts out of the tree
The label must be literal text: it is joined into the description at build time ("Gate, "). The value may be a "@textVariable" (the description follows it) or a text expression

Drawn text does not wrap or follow the system font scale, and has no bold: a line wider than the box is measured (textMeasure) and scaled down about its anchor, never cut off. Inline, the label and value shrink together
It fills its parent's width (fillMaxWidth) at a fixed height (stacked: 1.4 × label + 1.3 × value size; inline: 1.4 × the larger): in a row, put it in a weighted box, or it has no width

The value is onSurface and the label muted in every look, so mono needs no variant; a `color` like error is white (mono-dark) or black (mono-light) there, so do not let the colour alone carry a meaning

components.name: legend
components.title: Legend
components.prompt: Show a portfolio donut chart with a legend beside it naming each slice and its percent, and a two-column legend of traffic sources with their values.
teaches: Call {"Legend": {"values": "@shares", "labels": ["Stocks", "Bonds", "Cash", "Other"]}} with the name of a float array (export it and the host can replace the numbers) and one label per entry
Next to a DonutChart on the same array and colour, the swatches match the slices by index (the same tones: solid, then lighter); pass the donut's `color` when it is not primary
`format` prints each entry's share of the sum as a percent (default), the value itself, or nothing; `columns`: 2 lays the entries out in two weighted columns, alternating
Rows past the array's length collapse to 0 dp (a height expression over arrayLength), so a host that sends fewer values gets a shorter legend; labels are fixed when the document is built

snippets.note: the legend of the exported array shares, beside the DonutChart of the same array
each percent is round(100 * arrayGet(values, i) / sum) through textFromFloat merged with %
two weighted columns, the entries alternating; format value, the secondary colour and an accessibility label
each swatch is a rounded square whose paint alpha falls with its index, as the donut's slices do
the whole legend carries one contentDescription: the `label` given here, or "Legend: N entries" by default

shares.meaning: portfolio shares by asset, values >= 0, up to four (one per label)

check.describe: Top: a blue donut of four slices (solid to pale clockwise) with 100 in the centre and, beside it, four rows: a swatch in the slice's tone, Stocks 40%, Bonds 30%, Cash 20%, Other 10%, the percents right-aligned in muted. Below: two columns of violet swatches, Direct 58 and Search 27 on the left, Social 15, Email 8 and Referral 4 (Direct, Social, Referral left; Search, Email right). With shares [50, 30, 20] the fourth row collapses and the donut shows three slices. In mono the swatches alternate filled and outlined. At 234 dp the labels keep one line.

components.summary: A chart legend for a float array: one row per entry with a swatch in the series tone (the same colour sequence as DonutChart's slices, by index), the label in onSurface and its share of the sum as a percent (or the value) in muted at the end of the row; one or two columns, filling the width.
pitfalls: values is the name of a float array ("@shares" declared in resources.floatArrays), not a JSON list; labels is a JSON list written into the document ($each): a host can change the numbers but not the labels, so give one label per value the host may send. Rows past the array's length, or past maxEntries, collapse to 0 dp: each row's height is rowH * min(1, max(0, m - i)) over the local m = min(arrayLength(values), maxEntries), a tree variable at the head of the body. A visibility modifier cannot do this: it is an integer expression, which has no arrayLength and never sees a tree variable (U57), and the expander keeps a local that reads a float array out of resources.variables; a height expression is read at measure, in Java too (java-layout.sh: the collapsed row is 0 dp and the next content moves up). Each row clips to its bounds, so a collapsed swatch draws nothing

The swatches are the tones DonutChart gives its slices: paint alpha 1 - 0.7 * i / n over the same colour, so a Legend next to a DonutChart on the same array and `color` matches it by index. Pass the donut's `color` (secondary, success) when it is not primary. In mono the swatches alternate filled and outlined, as the donut's slices alternate thick and thin

The percent is round(100 * arrayGet(values, i) / sum) through textFromFloat (whole 3, decimal 0, flags 5) merged with "%"; rounded shares can add up to 99 or 101. format value prints the number with no decimals

columns 2 puts every entry in both columns and collapses the other column's half (an $if cannot test an index's parity), so a two-column legend costs twice the rows of a one-column one; use it for four to six short entries

Each row fills the width (the label sits in a weighted box, one line with an ellipsis, so a long label shortens instead of pushing the number out): in a row put the legend in a weighted box, or it has no width

components.name: line-chart
components.title: LineChart
components.prompt: Chart today's temperature hour by hour with the high and low marked, and a tide widget: the day's water level curve with high and low water, the hours under it, the metres beside it and a line at the current time.
teaches: Array mode: {"LineChart": {"values": "@temps", "x_min": 0, "x_max": 23}} draws a monotone spline through an exported float array, spread evenly over x
Function mode: "fn" is y as an expression of u (the x value), drawn with pathExpression over x_min..x_max; now: "timeInMin()" adds a line and a dot on the curve that follow the clock

Axis labels are text components: xLabels is a row under the plot (each centred on its x), yLabels a column beside it with a grid line per label; the canvas fills the width and derives every coordinate from componentWidth()/componentHeight()

snippets.note: bound to the exported float array temps, with extremes marked
a tide model as fn of u, drawn with pathExpression
now: timeInMin() and marks computed from tideHigh
fill: true inside a box with verticalWeight 1: the plot takes the card's remaining height

temps.meaning: hourly temperatures, any length >= 2, spread over x_min..x_max

tideAmp.meaning: tidal amplitude in metres (half the range)

tideHigh.meaning: minute of the day of the first high water

check.describe: Pinned clock 2026-10-30 15:00. Top card ('Temperature'): 24 hourly temperatures as an amber monotone curve over a light amber wash, grid lines at 20/15/10/5° lined up with the labels in the column on the left, hours 0h 6h 12h 18h 23h centred under their x, dots on the low (7.8° at 5 h) and the high (19.4° at 15 h); the header reads 7.8° – 19.4° from the array. Bottom card: the tide fn 1.6 + 1.2·cos((u − 312)·0.0084315) over 00..24 h fills the rest of the height: high water 2.8 m at 05:12 and 17:37, low 0.4 m at 11:25 and 23:50, each with a small dot (the fifth mark, 312 − 372.6, is before midnight and not drawn); a grey vertical line at 15:00 with a large dot on the rising curve at 1.9 m, which the header's '1.9 m now' matches. dark: the same on the dark palette; mono / mono-light: no wash, white (black) 2 dp lines and dots, grey grid. narrow (234) and wide (540): the plots and the x labels follow the width, the y labels keep their 32 dp column. shifted (tideHigh 600, a cooling day): high water moves to 10:00 and 22:25 and low water to 03:47 and 16:13, all four dotted (the marks list has five times; the ones outside 00..24 h are not drawn); the now dot sits on the falling side at 0.6 m, as the header says; the temperature curve falls from 19° to 6° with the extremes dotted at its ends and the header reads 6.0° – 19.0°.

components.summary: A value-over-time chart that fills its width: a smooth line through a float array or along a function of x, with an optional area fill, baseline, "now" marker, highlighted points and a cut-off (upTo) that draws the curve only so far today, and its axis labels as text components (a row under the chart, a column beside it).
pitfalls: Plotting a mathematical function (roots, turning points, a scrubbed point along it)? Use MathPlot: it finds roots and extrema on the server and labels them, and scales its axes. LineChart's fn mode is for data-like curves

A chart of today's values: now is "timeInMin()" (with x_min 0, x_max 1440), not a host variable set once; and whatever depends on now in the text around the chart (rising or falling, the next event, the current value) is computed from timeInMin() and the data too (see TIM examples), never typed in.

Which chart: LineChart for a value over time or over a range of x (a day of temperatures, a tide, a price, the sun's altitude) at card or screen width, with axis labels, a now marker or marked points; Sparkline for a word-sized trend beside a label (no axes, no labels); BarChart for separate quantities per category or period (steps per day, visits per week)

Don't hand-draw the chart on a canvas with literal coordinates and drawText labels: this component fills its width, derives every coordinate from componentWidth()/componentHeight() (named canvas variables), and puts its labels in text components, so it relayouts on resize and screen readers reach the labels

Two modes. values is the name of a float array ("@temps" in resources.floatArrays), not a JSON list: the curve is arraySpline through every value, spread evenly over x_min..x_max, so a host that sets the exported array redraws it, any length. fn is y as an expression of u, the x value (pathExpression's sample variable: write u, never x or a name of your own); it is spliced into the path's expressions, so it may read document variables and the clock ("@mean + @amp * cos((u - @high) * 0.0084315)"). Give one or the other

fn must stay within 20 expression entries (each number, variable, operator and function is one): the area path wraps it in 12 more and Android refuses a path expression over 32 entries with "Path too long" — json2rc and the Java parser write it anyway, so only a device shows the failure. Move constants into variables ("@k" is one entry; "2 * 3.14159 / 745.2" is five) and drop the area if needed

Function mode has no data to scale from: give y_min and y_max (default 0..1). Array mode scales to the array's own min..max unless you give them; a flat series sits on the top edge, and two charts only compare when they share y_min/y_max. Pass the same y_min/y_max the yLabels name: the labels are evenly spaced from y_max down to y_min and only the component's arithmetic, not the text, places the curve

xLabels are evenly spaced from x_min to x_max, each centred in an equal cell under its x, so the plot is inset by half a cell on each side (a 5-label axis on a 300 dp plot loses 30 dp per side); pick labels that divide the range evenly (0, 6, 12, 18, 24 h over 0..1440 min). A label at a data position ("High 05:12, 2.8 m") belongs in the caller's layout, a row of text above or below the chart, not on the canvas

now and marks put a dot on the curve itself: each is a two-point path at that x through the same function (a zero-length stroke with a round cap), so the dot follows the curve in either mode with nothing computed twice; now also draws a vertical line and is clamped to x_min..x_max; a mark outside x_min..x_max is not drawn (its dot is moved off the canvas). marks is a list fixed in length when the document is built, but each item may be an expression ("@high + 372.6"). A literal 0 for now, baseline, y_min or y_max counts as given

baseline draws a line at that value (0 °C, mean sea level, the horizon) and the area then fills between the curve and it, above and below; without it the area fills to the bottom of the plot. extremes (array mode) dots the first sample equal to the array's max and the first equal to its min, and none on a flat series

A curve of today so far (solar production, usage): pass the whole day as values, x_min..x_max the whole day, and upTo the sample index of now, e.g. "(timeInMin() - @x_min) / 45" for 33 samples 45 min apart (with now: "timeInMin()" for the marker). The line and area end at the interpolated point and the rest of the axis stays empty. Never fake it by pushing future samples below y_min or clipping the canvas: that leaves a vertical stroke at now and forces area off. Future samples may hold anything (0, a forecast); they are not drawn and do not count for extremes, but they still scale the plot when y_min/y_max are not given, so give y_min/y_max for a stable scale
Mono drops the area wash (no alpha fills on AOD or e-ink) and draws the line in onSurface at 2 dp; the grid, baseline and now line stay the one grey

The body declares named canvas variables and paths, so every call is expanded (about 1.1 KB for a function chart, 1.6 KB with both label rows), never a pattern: fine for the one or two charts a screen shows

components.name: list-detail
components.title: ListDetail: a master list and the selected item, one pane or two
components.prompt: Make a settings screen with categories in a list and the chosen category's settings: one pane on a phone with a back arrow, list and detail side by side on a tablet.
teaches: Give items as objects: {"title", "subtitle", "preview", "meta", "lead", "body", "detail"}. The component owns the rest: one pane or two, the selection, the highlight and back
Under 600 dp a row tap opens the detail with a back arrow; from 600 dp the list is a third of the width and a tap changes the detail in place
detail is any node, here KeyValueRows holding Switches; bind selected and open to resources variables to preset or read them

snippets.note: the whole call: four categories and their settings
a detail is any node: rows with switches
each row is one labelled tap target, read as title and subtitle

open.meaning: 1: the detail is open on a phone

check.describe: Phone (360x640, 640 wide is two panes): Settings and four rows, each an icon, a name and a summary. phone-detail: a back arrow and Settings, then Network with Wi-Fi on and Bluetooth off. Landscape, tablet and desktop: the list on the left with Network highlighted by a bar and a tint, a rule, Network's settings on the right. tap-sound: Sound highlighted and its settings shown.

components.summary: A whole list-detail screen from data: a master list (a title, then rows with a lead, title, subtitle, preview and a time or value) and the selected item's detail. On a phone one pane shows: the list, and a tap opens the detail with a back arrow. From 600 dp wide both panes show side by side, the list about a third (260 to 420 dp), the selected row highlighted, and a tap changes the detail in place.
pitfalls: Give items as data and let it decide: under wideAt (600 dp) one pane, the list or (open = 1) the detail with a back arrow; from wideAt both panes, the list listShare of the width (260 to 420 dp) and the selected row highlighted with a tint and a bar on its start edge (the bar alone in mono). Decided by the window width, never by content

Every item's detail is written into the document and shown by visibility: the doc grows with items x detail. Fine for tens of items; for a long or app-fed list, keep detail small, put shared actions in detailEnd (written once) and read the selected variable there

A host action name used in more than one place (a Button with addToCart in every item's detail) makes json2rc and the Java parser write different bytes. Put the action once in detailEnd and send the index: {"type": "hostNamedAction", "name": "addToCart", "value": "@sel", "valueType": "float", "actionType": 0}

Rows have fixed heights from their fields: 52 dp with a title only, 64 with a subtitle, 62 + 18 per preview line with a preview. Title, subtitle and preview are one line each (ellipsized); meta, a time or price, is not cut: keep it short

body is plain text that wraps, \n for a line break, blank lines between paragraphs. With headline (an email subject) the headline is the big line and the header shows the lead, title and meta only, so the subject is not said twice
lead is any node, drawn in the row and again in the detail header: an Avatar or Icon of about 40 dp. A lead on a surfaceHigh tile loses its edge on the selected row, which is surfaceHigh too
selected is from 0 and open is 0/1: bind resources variables ("@sel", "@open") to preset a phone on the detail or to read the selection. Do not name a variable step

Both panes scroll on their own; the detail's scroll position is shared by all items, so a long message scrolled down leaves the next one scrolled too. There is no system back: the back arrow is the only way back on a phone
width and height default to the window: pass them when it is not the whole window. The list sits on surface, the detail on background (set background to change it)

components.name: list-item
components.title: ListItem
components.prompt: Make a list row with a contact's avatar, name and role, and a chevron that opens their details when tapped.
teaches: Call {"ListItem": {"title": "Ada Lovelace", "subtitle": "Analyst", "chevron": true, "onClick": {...}}}: the whole 64 dp row is the tap target, with a ripple
Put an Avatar or icon in slots.leading and a control (a Switch) in slots.trailing; both are optional
Use padding 0 inside a Card, which already pads its content; the default 16 lines up with a full-width screen

snippets.note: a clickable row: onClick sets opened to 1
an Avatar in the leading slot
the weighted text column pushes the trailing Switch to the end
title only; the title is also the row's accessibility label

check.describe: Three 64 dp rows: Ada Lovelace with an AL avatar, Analyst and a chevron; Do not disturb with its subtitle and a switch, tapped on in the render; About this phone with a chevron. Rows fill the width with the text column weighted: at 200 dp the long subtitle ends in … while the avatar, switch and chevrons keep their size (the switch is tapped at its new place), at 540 dp the trailing items move to the end.

components.summary: A 64 dp list row: optional leading content (an Avatar, an icon), a title with an optional subtitle, optional trailing content or a built-in chevron, and an optional click.
pitfalls: Spacers, not spacedBy, separate the weighted text column from the slots: weights ignore spacedBy

Title and subtitle are one line each with an ellipsis: the text column is the weighted child, so in a narrow row it shortens with … and the slots and chevron keep their size, instead of the title wrapping out of the 64 dp row
Separate rows with a Divider whose inset is padding + 56 (lines it up with the text after a 40 dp Avatar): 72 by default, 56 with padding 0 in a Card

components.name: map-list
components.title: MapList: places on a map and in a list, stacked or side by side
components.prompt: Show our five offices worldwide as numbered markers on a map with a list of them below (city, team, time zone). On a wide screen put the list in a side panel and let the map fill the rest. Tapping a row or a marker selects that office.
teaches: Give places as objects: {"title", "subtitle", "meta", "metaIcon", "place", "mark"}, place a city name or "lon,lat". The component owns the rest: the map framed to the places, numbered markers, the list, the selection and the adaptation
Phone or portrait tablet: header, map (42% of the height) and list stacked; from 600 dp and landscape the list is a 280-360 dp side panel and the map fills the rest
A row tap and a marker tap set the same selected variable: the row gets a tint and a bar, the marker grows with a halo. Bind it ("@sel") to preset or read it

snippets.note: the whole call: five offices
one place: a row and a marker that both select it
each row is one labelled tap target

check.describe: Phone: Offices and a subtitle, a world map with five numbered blue markers (London enlarged with a halo), a rule, then five rows: a number disc, city, team and UTC offset; London tinted with a bar. 640x360 and 1280x800: the list in a left panel, the map filling the right. 800x1280: stacked like the phone, bigger. tap-marker: Tokyo's marker enlarged and its row highlighted. desktop-tap-row: São Paulo selected.

components.summary: A whole map-and-list screen from data: places as numbered markers on a map (WorldMap, framed to fit them or a given region) and the same places as a list (a number, a name, a detail, a distance or rating). On a phone or a tall window the map is on top (about 42% of the height) and the list under it; on a wide window (from 600 dp and landscape) the list is a side panel on the left (280 to 360 dp) and the map fills the rest. Tapping a row selects it and enlarges its marker; tapping a marker selects its row.
pitfalls: Give places as data and let it decide: under wideAt (600 dp), or when the window is not clearly landscape (width under 1.2 x height, a portrait tablet), the header, the map (mapShare of the height under it) and the list stack; otherwise the list is a side panel (38% of the width, 280 to 360 dp) and the map fills the rest. Decided by the window, never by content

place is a city name from Natural Earth's 1,250 places (capitals, state capitals, large cities; the error names a missing one) or "lon,lat" as ONE string ("12.57,55.68"). An array [lon, lat] is flattened by the expander and fails

The map frames the places tightly (WorldMap fit) at every size; markers are 22 dp discs, so places closer than about 30 dp on the smallest map overlap: on a phone a 360 dp wide map, so keep places at least ~1/12 of the frame's width apart. There is no street or city-level map: pick places a world or continent map can show (cities, stores across a country or continent, offices worldwide, a road trip's stops), not shops in one town
