snippets.note: bound to guests, 1..8: the render taps + once
the buttons set min(@max, @guests + @step) and max(@min, @guests - @step)
half-kilo steps, the value printed with one decimal

check.describe: Guests reads 3 after the render's tap on + (it starts at 2); Weight, kg reads 2.5; tapping − on weight shows 2.0. The steppers keep their size at the end of each row and the labels sit in weighted boxes: at 234 dp "Weight, kg" ends in …, at 540 dp the labels keep their place and the + tap still lands.

components.summary: A minus / value / plus control that changes a number by `step`, clamped to [min, max], then runs `onDecrement` or `onIncrement` (and any `onClick`). Each button is a 36 dp circle in a 48 dp touch target.
pitfalls: textFromFloat `whole` is the number of integer digits kept, not a minimum: whole 1 prints 10 as 0. The value uses whole 3 with flags 5 (no padding), so it stays centred
The buttons clamp with max(@min, @value - @step) and min(@max, @value + @step): a value outside [min, max] set by the host is pulled back on the next tap
The buttons are announced as Decrease and Increase, followed by `label` when given ("Decrease guests"); put the stepper next to a KeyValueRow key that names the quantity

`onDecrement` / `onIncrement` run after the clamped step of their own button, `onClick` after both: an app reading the exported `value` on a hostNamedAction sees the new number (and is told even when a tap at min or max changed nothing)
Give a hostNamedAction to onIncrement / onDecrement, never to onClick: a named action written in two click lists is registered with the first list only, so the other button sends it with no name
Each button is a 36 dp circle inside 6 dp of padding, so its click target is 48 × 48 dp; the whole stepper is 148 × 48 dp, with 12 dp of visible space between a circle and the number

components.name: steps
components.title: Steps
components.prompt: A package delivery tracker: the steps Ordered, Shipped, Out for delivery and Delivered in a row, done ones ticked, the current one highlighted, followed by a compact four-step checkout indicator and a vertical three-step order history.
teaches: Call {"Steps": {"steps": ["Ordered", "Shipped", "Out for delivery", "Delivered"], "current": "@stage"}}: the labels are a static list, current a 0-based index the app sets (steps before it are done, after it to do)
Horizontal (the default) fills its parent's width with the dots evenly spaced and the labels under them; orientation vertical stacks the dots with the labels beside them and wraps its content
size sets the dot diameter, showLabels false keeps only the dots, and label overrides the accessibility description ("Step N of M" by default)

snippets.note: bound to the exported variable stage (2): two ticked discs, a haloed current disc, an outlined last one, joined by connectors
the canvas reads componentWidth() / n as the pitch between dots, so the row follows its parent's width
a literal current (1) with 18 dp dots and an explicit accessibility label
vertical, all three done but the last: each label is a muted and an onSurface copy swapped by visibility

stage.meaning: current delivery step, 0 Ordered to 3 Delivered

check.describe: Under the title and 'Order #4821', four dots across the width: Ordered and Shipped are blue discs with a white tick joined by a blue line, Out for delivery a blue disc with a pale blue halo and a bold dark label, Delivered a grey outlined disc on a grey line; setting stage to 3 ticks the third and fills the fourth. Below, 'Checkout' over a smaller four-step row at its second step (Cart ticked, Address haloed), then 'History' over a vertical column of three dots with Ordered and Packed ticked and Shipped haloed. Mono draws done as white discs with a black tick, current as a ring with a dot inside, to do as a grey ring (black on white in mono light). At 234 dp the four-step rows keep four dots that shrink slightly and 'Out for delivery' wraps; at 540 dp the dots spread out.

components.summary: Progress steps (an order's Ordered / Shipped / Out for delivery / Delivered, a wizard's pages): a dot per step joined by connectors, done steps a filled primary disc with a check mark, the current one a primary disc with a halo, the rest outlined in muted; the connector is primary up to the current step. Labels under the dots (horizontal, filling the width) or beside them (vertical).
pitfalls: steps is static: the dots and labels are generated when the document is built ($each), and their number is the local n ({"$count": "steps"}); current is the run-time part, a float the app sets ("@stage")

Each step's look is three drawings switched by paint alpha over k = clamp(0, n - 1, round(current)): to do step(i - k, 0.5), done step(k - i, 0.5), current 1 - min(1, abs(k - i)). step(x, edge) is x > edge (strict), so the edges sit at ±0.5. A literal current folds every alpha to 0 or 1

The connector is one grey segment per gap (between dot edges, clipped at the last dot's centre) under one primary line from the first dot to the current one, which the filled dots cover: the to-do dots are hollow, so the track is drawn in segments rather than erased

Horizontal fills the parent's width: the canvas reads p = componentWidth() / n and s = min(1, p / size) into two variables, then draws each segment and each dot in a frame translated by p per step (a translate of @p, not a per-dot expression), so a narrow box shrinks the dots instead of overlapping them. In a row put it in a weighted box, or it has no width. Labels sit in weighted boxes of the same pitch and wrap when long
Vertical has a fixed geometry: a size + 8 wide canvas, rows of size + 16, labels in boxes of that height beside each dot; it wraps its content (no fillMaxWidth)

Each label is two text nodes, muted and onSurface bold, swapped by visibility (integer expressions over k, exact 0 or 1, as TextChoice): about 180 B per step with its string stored once. showLabels false drops them

Mono shows state by shape: done a filled disc with a check in onPrimary, current a ring with a smaller disc inside (no alpha wash), to do an outline; the track is 1.5 dp grey. The layout is the same in every look, so one call site serves light, dark, mono and mono-light

The accessibility description is "Step N of M" (textMerge over textFromFloat(k + 1)), not the step's name: the Java reference parser cannot name a data list (U4), so a textLookup of the label by index would not convert there; pass `label` when the description should carry more

components.name: sweep-trace
components.title: SweepTrace
components.prompt: Show live ECG, pleth and respiration waveforms that sweep across the screen and erase ahead of themselves like a bedside monitor, at a heart rate the app sets.
teaches: One cycle in a float array and a rate: {"SweepTrace": {"values": "@ecg", "rate": "@hr / 60", "window": 0.62}}; the array is repeated at the rate, so a host variable re-times it live
window keeps a sharp shape its real width: the beat is stored as 0.62 s and the baseline fills the rest of each cycle, so 150 bpm reads as tachycardia rather than a squashed beat
No buffer: the sample at x shows time T - fract((head - x) / W + 1) * W / speed, two pathExpressions (before the head and after the gap) on a fixed sample grid
delay lags one trace behind another (pleth after ECG); speed 25 gives a slow respiration sweep

snippets.note: ECG with a fixed-width beat window and a glow
pleth trailing the heartbeat by 0.18 cycles
a slow sweep at 25 dp/s
one cycle per wave
the sweep loops with the clock

check.describe: Title 'Live waveforms', then three traces each with a label at the top left, an erase gap and a head dot: a green ECG with narrow R waves (glow), a blue pulse wave with a dicrotic notch, an amber breathing wave sweeping four times slower. Two seconds later the heads have moved 200 dp (50 dp for breathing). hr 150: twice as many beats, same QRS width. Mono: white or black lines, no glow, the head steps once a second.

components.summary: A live waveform that sweeps left to right and overwrites itself, like a patient monitor or an oscilloscope: one cycle of a float array repeated at a rate, drawn up to a moving head with an erase gap ahead of it, rebuilt every frame from the clock.
pitfalls: values is the NAME of a float array holding one cycle; repeat its first value at the end, or the trace jumps at every cycle seam
Nothing is stored: each frame redraws the visible sweep from the clock, so changing rate re-times the history already on screen once, and continuousSec() wraps at the hour (one jump an hour)
In mono (always-on, e-ink) the clock is timeInSec(): the head steps forward once a second instead of gliding, and there is no glow
For sharp waves keep sample 1 and use window: a QRS stored as a fraction of the cycle aliases (peaks of varying height) at high rates
The trace repaints every frame (continuousSec()); put one or a few on a screen, not dozens
The TypeScript player cannot evaluate splineLoop inside a pathExpression (no op 75 in PathExpression.evalRPN), which is why the trace uses spline(fract(...))

components.name: swipe-stack
components.title: SwipeStack: a stack of cards to swipe right to like or left to pass
components.prompt: Show tonight's dinner ideas as a Tinder-style card stack: swipe right for yum, left to pass, with buttons and a count of each.
teaches: Draw each card in the card slot from the index variable you name ("index": "@card"): per-card colours, sizes and arrays read @card, and per-card texts are drawn once each and shown with alpha 1 - min(1, abs(@card - j))

Bind liked, passed and decision to resources variables to show the counts and to send the last verdict to the app in onSwipe (a hostAction carrying @verdict: +(i + 1) liked, -(i + 1) passed, 0 sprang back)
Wrap the call in a box with verticalWeight to give it the space under a header; the card keeps its design aspect and scales to fit

snippets.note: the whole call: four recipe cards, counts and a host action; drag, fling and spring-back are built in
the verdict sent to the app after each release or button tap
the card slot, drawn from @card for every card in the stack, the one flying away included

check.describe: Tonight's dinner, 0 liked · 0 passed, a stack of recipe cards (Ramen on top, Tacos and Paella behind) and Pass / Like buttons. Dragging right tilts Ramen, fades in YUM and lifts Tacos. A flick flies Ramen off and the header reads 1 liked; a slow drag springs back; the Pass button flings the top card left. Mono: outlined cards, an outlined stamp and outlined buttons; no motion after release.

components.java_difference: the onSwipe hostAction name (swipe) is used three times, by the swipe release and both buttons: json2rc declares it once before the tree so every one sends it (Parser.ts EXTENSION, EXAMPLES_FINDINGS U58); the Java parser writes it inside the first action list only. Without onSwipe the bytes are identical
components.summary: A Tinder-style stack of cards you swipe: the top card follows the finger and tilts, a like or pass stamp fades in and the card behind scales up; a flick or a drag past the threshold flies it off left or right with its release speed, anything else springs back with a damped spring. Optional Pass / Like buttons fling it too. Each card is drawn by the card slot from the index variable; counts and the last decision are variables, and onSwipe can tell the host.
pitfalls: One SwipeStack per document: its paths (swsCard, swsHeart) have fixed names
The card slot is drawn for every visible card each frame: keep it to a few dozen commands and use loops and float arrays, not one copy per card
Choose texts per card by alpha, not textLookup: Java's addDataList drops the list id, so textLookup cannot reach it from JSON
A paint color resets alpha: write the alpha after the colour in each paint that fades
onSwipe also runs for a spring-back and a plain tap, with decision 0: test the sign of decision in the app
Taps on the buttons are ignored for 0.3 s after a fling, so two cards never fly at once
Mono has no motion: a fling or a spring-back settles at once, the drag still follows the finger

components.name: switch
components.title: Switch
components.prompt: Add an on/off toggle switch for Wi-Fi next to its label, like in a settings screen.
teaches: Call {"Switch": {"label": "Wi-Fi", "checked": "@wifi"}} and declare wifi (0 or 1) in resources.variables: a tap flips it, and the rest of the document can read or preset it
Leave `checked` out and the switch keeps its own state, starting off; `color` sets the track colour when on
Put the visible label beside it (a text and a weighted spacer box in a row) and pass the same words as `label`

snippets.note: a Switch bound to the document variable wifi, which starts on
unbound, with a green track: it keeps its own state (tapped on in the render)
label is the accessibility label; the visible Bluetooth text sits beside it

check.describe: Wi-Fi is on (blue), Bluetooth off (grey); the render taps Battery saver, which slides on with a green track. Switches stay at the end of their rows and the labels sit in weighted boxes: at 160 dp "Battery saver" ends in …, at 540 dp the switches move to the right edge (the tap follows them).

components.summary: An on/off switch: a tap flips its variable (0 or 1), then runs any extra `onClick` actions; the thumb springs across (a little overshoot) while the track colour fades in. A screen reader hears the label and the state, On or Off, which follows the value: no extra On/Off text is needed.
pitfalls: The motion is paint time: an animated local p = {"value": "@checked", "anim": 0.3} eases from 0 to 1 when the state flips (Java re-evaluates an animated expression every frame while it runs), and the thumb x is 16 + 20 * (p + 0.5 * sin(pi * p) * (2 * @checked - 1)): the sine term pushes it about 10% past the end and back, the spring feel. No layout runs while it moves
The track colour follows the state without colour expressions: the `color` track is drawn over the grey one with paint alpha p
Mono themes have no motion: p is @checked itself, so the thumb and the track snap (the sine term is 0 at both ends)
It draws no text: put the visible label next to it (a KeyValueRow key, a ListItem title) and pass the same words as `label`

A switch that drives something outside the document (a light, a lock) needs more than its exported variable: pass the app's hostNamedAction in `onClick` (it runs after the flip, so the exported value is already the new state when the app reads it)

Accessibility: one node, the transparent box laid over the drawing, carries the label (contentDescription), the state (stateDescription) and the click. The state text is cut from "Off On " by textSubtext at 4 * checked and trimmed (textTransform 3) in the canvas's global section, so it follows the value at run time; the box comes after the canvas because the parsers bind the name in document order. The JSON semantics has no role key (role is always unset), so no 'switch' role. About 125 B per call, and the named text ops keep the switch from compiling to a pattern (mono galleries grow more)

components.name: tabs
components.title: Tabs
components.prompt: Add a Day / Week / Month tab bar whose selected tab is highlighted with an underline, and the same choice as a segmented control (a pill track with the selected option filled).
teaches: Call {"Tabs": {"labels": ["Day", "Week", "Month"], "selected": "@tab"}}: the labels are static, a tap sets tab to the tab's index
"style": "segmented" draws a segmented control instead: a pill track, the selected option a filled primary pill that slides (mono: a white pill on a grey-ringed black track)
Bind a document variable (tab, 0 here) so panels and PagerDots can follow the selection; a tap on a tab sets it to that tab's index
Each tab announces its label and Selected or Not selected, following the bound variable at run time
Panels below follow the same variable (graphicsLayer alpha 1 - min(1, abs(@tab - i))); the bar does not switch content itself

snippets.note: three tabs bound to the document variable tab (the render taps Week)
equal-width tabs: each is a weight 1 box
each label is also its tab's accessibility label
a segmented control bound to view (Month preset): each option announces Selected or Not selected

check.describe: The render taps Week on the underline bar: it lights up in blue with the underline under it; Day and Month are muted. Below, the segmented control has Month (view = 2) as a filled blue pill with a white label on a light grey pill track, Day and Week in dark text. The tabs share the width by weight and the underline and pill are fractions of componentWidth(): at 234 and 540 dp the middle tap still selects Week and both bars fit. Mono: Month is a white pill with black text on a black track ringed in grey.

components.summary: A 48 dp row of equal-width tabs from a static list of labels: a tap sets `selected` to the tab's index (then runs any extra `onClick` actions). style underline (default) slides an underline under the selected tab; style segmented is a pill-shaped track whose filled pill slides to the selected option (a segmented control: Day / Week / Month). A screen reader hears each tab's label and Selected or Not selected, which follows the index at run time.
pitfalls: labels is static: the tabs are generated when the document is built ($each), and their number is the local n ({"$count": "labels"}); the selection is the runtime part

The motion is an animated local s = {"value": "@selected", "anim": 0.25}: it eases to the new index at paint time, and everything visible reads s, not @selected (the tap still sets @selected at once, so panels can switch immediately)
Each tab's highlight is a second, coloured copy of its label over the plain one, with graphicsLayer alpha 1 - min(1, abs(s - i)): 1 on the selected tab, 0 elsewhere, a cross-fade while s moves

underline: one 2 dp canvas under the row, a rect from s * componentWidth() / n to (s + 1) * componentWidth() / n, so it slides between tabs. segmented: one canvas behind the row draws the pill the same way (a round rect inset 4 dp), so it slides too
Mono themes have no motion: s is @selected, the underline, the pill and the highlight jump
Show the matching panel with the same alpha expression on stacked panels (or visibility); the tab bar does not switch content by itself

`onClick` actions are appended to every tab's click list, after the valueFloatChange: a hostNamedAction carrying "@sel" (valueType float) sends the tapped index, and tapping the selected tab again sends it too. valueType is a json2rc extension: the Java JSON parser does not write the value

Accessibility: each tab carries its label (contentDescription), the state (stateDescription, Selected or Not selected) and the click; the whole 48 dp height of each tab is the touch target. The state is cut from "Not selectedSelected    " by textSubtext at 12 * (1 - min(1, abs(@selected - i))) and trimmed (as in Chip), in the global section of a 0-size canvas at the head of the bar, so it follows a bound variable at run time. About 120 B per tab, and the named text ops keep the call from compiling to a pattern
Segmented: each tab's tap area is the inset pill (padding 4, clip 20), so the press ripple stays inside the pill's rounded shape.

components.name: text-choice
components.title: Text choice
components.prompt: Show a word picked at run time from a fixed list: the moon phase name from a phase variable, today's weekday name from the clock, and a Rising / Falling tide pill from a 0/1 variable, each laid out like a normal text in a row.
teaches: {"TextChoice": {"items": ["Rising", "Falling"], "index": "@falling"}} shows one of the items, picked by a 0-based index that may be a variable or an expression

A layout text cannot take textSubtext or textLookup in Java, so the choice is one text per item, each with a visibility that is exactly 1 for its index and 0 (GONE) otherwise: only the shown item takes space

The visibility is an integer expression, 1 - min(1, abs(k - i)), over k = clamp(0, n - 1, round(index)), a float expression computed once per call; the player keeps a float's truncated int, which is why k is rounded first
Weekday names need weekDay() - 1 (weekDay() is 1 for Monday); a fraction of a cycle becomes an index with round(@phase * 8) % 8

snippets.note: eight moon phase names chosen by round(@phase * 8) % 8 (0.6 shows Waning gibbous)
the weekday name from weekDay() - 1
Rising / Falling from a 0/1 variable inside a pill that sizes to the word shown

check.describe: On Thursday 29 October 2026 with phase 0.6 and falling 0: "Moon: Waning gibbous tonight", "Today is Thursday here" (blue) and "Tide [Rising] at 14:05" with the pill sized to Rising. The switched render (phase 0.97, falling 1, Sunday 1 November 2026) reads "New moon" (round(7.76) % 8 wraps to 0), "Sunday" and a wider "Falling" pill; the full render (phase 0.5, Monday 2 November) reads "Full moon" and "Monday". In every row the next text follows the shown word directly, so the hidden items take no space. The rows size to their content: at 240 dp the moon row still fits and at 420 dp nothing moves.

components.summary: One of several fixed texts, picked at run time by an index (a variable or an expression): a phase name, a weekday, a status word such as Rising / Falling, laid out like a plain text.
pitfalls: Use it for a word or phrase from a fixed set chosen at run time (a phase name, a weekday, Rising / Falling, Open / Closed). For a number use textFromFloat; to join a fixed text and a live one use textMerge; for a text the host sends, a text variable

A layout `text` cannot take textSubtext, textTransform or textLookup itself (the Java parser accepts them only among canvas commands), so a name cut out of one string by index needs a canvas command first (see the long-list note); this component needs nothing but layout texts
index is 0-based: weekDay() is 1 (Monday) to 7, so pass "weekDay() - 1"; a fraction of a cycle (a moon phase 0..1) needs "round(@phase * 8) % 8" or similar, not the fraction itself
index is rounded to the nearest whole number and clamped to 0..n-1, so a stray value shows the first or last item, never nothing and never two

It is always expanded, never a definePattern template: a text inside a pattern shares its component id across inflations in shipped Java runtimes (U7). Each call costs about 90 B per item plus its string (Rising / Falling: 174 B; seven weekday names: 713 B)
A literal index works but is pointless (use a plain text); the index is meant to be a variable or an expression that changes

For a long list (more than about 8 items: 31 day numbers, 60 minutes, 12 months on a small budget), cut the name from one padded string instead: a 0-size canvas whose `global` section holds textSubtext (start "(weekDay() - 1) * 9", len 9, varName dayName9) and a textTransform trim (operation 3, varName dayName), then a layout text {"value": "@dayName"}. The global section runs before the layout, so the layout text can read the variable (STR-05 hoists data the same way); seven weekdays cost about 180 B that way, whatever the count. Every name must be padded to the same width

Each item is its own text node; all but one are GONE (visibility 0), so the box takes the size of the one shown and changes size when the choice changes. In a row, neighbours move; give it a fixed width if they shouldn't

The visibility of each item is an INTEGER expression (1 - min(1, abs(k - i)), exact 0 or 1) over the float index k: the player stores a float as its truncated int, so k is rounded first. A float expression that comes out 0.999 would hide every item
Accessibility reads the visible item only (hidden items are GONE), so no label is needed

components.name: timeline-track
components.title: TimelineTrack
components.prompt: Show today's bookings for three meeting rooms from 9 to 5, with overlapping bookings stacked and a line at the current time.
teaches: Call {"TimelineTrack": {"items": [{start, end, label, lane, category}], "now": "clock"}}: overlapping items in a lane stack into rows
Labels show in full when the bar is wide enough, beside a short bar when there is room, else the initial
A legend names the categories; a red line follows the clock

snippets.note: bars and gaps are weights in rows
now: clock
full label, initial or beside, by visibility

check.describe: 09:00 to 17:00 across, three rooms; Room B has two rows (the workshop overlaps the hiring panel); coloured bars with labels or initials; a red line at 14:30; a legend.

components.summary: A schedule or timeline laid out by the server: name intervals (start, end, label, optional lane such as a person or room, optional category for the colour) and it packs overlapping ones into rows, draws a time axis with ticks, a legend for the categories, and a red now line that can follow the device clock. Labels show in full, as an initial, beside a short bar, or not at all, by the space each bar gets.
pitfalls: Write every time in one form: "Mon 09:00" and "09:00" can't mix
Its height is its content (axis, rows, legend): put it in a scrolling column if there are many lanes
In a week view on a phone, an 8-hour bar is about 12 dp wide: labels give way to the category initial or nothing, so use category (and the legend) for what matters
now: "clock" uses weekDay() and timeInMin(): a week axis must start on Monday 00:00 for the line to land right
About 120 to 250 B per interval (two texts: the full label and its initial) plus the axis

components.name: top-bar
components.title: TopBar
components.prompt: Put an app bar at the top of the screen with a back arrow, the title Settings and a search button on the right.
teaches: Call {"TopBar": {"title": "Inbox"}} for a 56 dp bar that fills the width, on @colors.surface
Put a back or menu icon button in slots.navigation and icon buttons in slots.actions: the actions are pushed to the end
Make each icon button a 40 dp clipped box with a ripple, a semantics contentDescription and an onClick, around a 20 dp canvas icon

snippets.note: the default call: a title only
a labelled 40 dp back button, centred icon
a search action, pushed to the end by the bar's weighted spacer

check.describe: Two bars: Inbox alone, and Settings with a back arrow before the title and a magnifier at the right end; tapping them sets action to 1 and 2. The bars fill the width: at 160 dp "Settings" ends in … and the search action stays on screen, at 540 dp the action moves to the end.

components.summary: An app bar: optional navigation content, a title, and actions pushed to the end.
pitfalls: The title sits in the weighted box (weight 1; the text is one line with an ellipsis): it pushes the actions to the end and, in a narrow bar, shortens with … instead of pushing them off the edge. Weight the box, not the text: the C++ player gives a weighted text its full width and squeezes the actions to nothing. The bar is 56 dp tall and fills its width
Icon buttons in the slots need their own semantics contentDescription and a 40 to 48 dp box: a bare canvas is neither labelled nor easy to hit

components.name: transportcontrols
components.title: Transport controls
components.prompt: Playback controls: previous, play or pause, next, shuffle and repeat, each telling the app and announcing its state.
teaches: Each control has its own action; a tap flips the state at once and the app confirms
Repeat's three states differ by weight: grey, tinted disc, solid disc with the 1

snippets.note: the call
the call
the call
the call
the call
the call
the call
the call

check.describe: Top row: shuffle in a tinted disc, previous, a large filled pause, next, grey repeat. Lower row: back 10, a smaller play, forward 30. Mono: a ring for shuffle on.

components.summary: Media transport row: previous, a filled play/pause that cross-fades as it flips, next, and optionally shuffle and repeat with three clearly different states (off grey, all a tinted disc, one a solid disc). Each control sends its own host action, flips its own state at once and tells a screen reader its state; shuffle and repeat drop out when the window is narrow.
pitfalls: Host action names must differ per control when the document must also convert with the Java parser (U58): playPause, previous, next, shuffle, repeat
The tap writes the bound variable first, so the icon flips at once; the app then confirms by writing the same variable. An app that refuses the change just writes it back

To send a state to the app, carry it: {"type": "hostNamedAction", "name": "repeat", "value": "@repeat", "valueType": "float", "actionType": 0} (both keys: json2rc reads valueType, the Java parser actionType, same bytes)

It fills the width it is given and spaces its controls evenly: three controls need 144 dp at size small, 160 at medium, five need 256 at medium. secondaryAt is compared with the WINDOW, so in a side-by-side pane raise it: secondaryAt can be an expression. Under 140 dp of window only play/pause stays
One call per document is the normal case. Its label variables are shared names (tcPlayLabel, tcShufLabel, tcRepLabel): two calls with different state would read each other's label on the first frame
Screen reader: Play or Pause as a live label; shuffle reads On or Off as state, repeat Off, All or One track. Mono: state by shape, ring for on and a solid disc for repeat one. No motion in mono

components.name: trendsparkline
components.title: TrendSparkline
components.prompt: Small trends in rows that are green when they ended up, red when they ended down, grey when flat.
teaches: Call {"TrendSparkline": {"values": "@week"}}: colour compares the latest with the first value, or with baseline
A flat series sits in the middle, and moves under minRange stay small

snippets.note: bound to an exported array
with a dashed baseline
see the call
see the call

check.describe: Green rising, red falling, grey level line each ending on a dot, and a wider one with a dashed baseline.

components.summary: A word-sized trend for a row or a tile: a line through a float array that is green when it ended up, red when it ended down and grey when flat, with a dot on the latest value, a faint wash and an optional dashed baseline. A flat series sits in the middle, and tiny moves stay small.
pitfalls: Sparkline is a plain trend in one colour, scaled to min and max. Use this one when up or down means something: stocks, sales, usage
Colour compares the latest value with the baseline, or with the first value: it answers 'did this end higher', not 'is the line going up now'
In mono both directions are one colour: put a Delta beside it for the direction; the dot still marks the end
Each call costs about 1 KB: fine for a watchlist of ten, heavy beyond that

components.name: twocolumns
components.title: TwoColumns
components.prompt: Show two sets of sections side by side when wide and one under the other when narrow, each as tall as its content, on a scrolling screen.
teaches: slots.first and slots.second each take a list of sections
inset says how much padding the page has taken from the window

snippets.note: the two columns

check.describe: At 320 wide, the first card over the second, 12 dp apart. From 560 wide, the two side by side, tops aligned, each as tall as its content.

components.summary: Two columns of sections, side by side when the window is wide and one under the other when it is not. Each is as tall as its content, so it belongs on a scrolling screen; each part is written once, not once per layout. For two parts that fill a fixed window, use AdaptiveSplit.
pitfalls: inset must match the padding around the call: flow wraps as soon as the two widths exceed the real space, and the columns stack on a wide screen
Decided by the window, not by content: a tall first column stays tall, with empty space under the shorter one
The slots cannot read s: to change content by layout, compute the same flag in the document

components.name: walkthrough
components.title: Walkthrough
components.prompt: Explain why a² + b² = c² in four steps: a drawing of a 3-4-5 triangle whose squares grow in one by one, a title and a sentence per step, Back / Next (Start over on the last step), "Step 2 of 4" with dots, and a play button that advances every three seconds.
teaches: Call {"Walkthrough": {"step": "@step", "shown": "@stepNow", "eased": "@stepEased", "titles": [...], "texts": [...], "slots": {"content": [DRAWING]}}}: the drawing reads @stepNow (the step on screen) or @stepEased (the same, eased over 0.6 s) and the walkthrough supplies caption, progress, Back / Next and autoplay
A component publishes a value by declaring a tree variable named after the caller's variable ({"$name": "shown"}): readable in the content slot or anywhere after the call, never declared in resources
Morph a drawing between steps from one eased number: grow the k-th element with clamp(0, 1, @stepEased - (k - 1)), so the square on b grows while the step goes from 1 to 2 and stays full after

Autoplay without a timer and without a clock listener: the step on screen is step + playing × (min(last, s0 + floor((animationTime() − t0) / interval)) − step); Play stores s0 and t0 = animationTime(), Pause writes the step on screen back into step. Frames come from an animated local whose target, run × floor(animationTime() × 2), changes every half second while playing, so a paused or finished walkthrough is idle

The caption is one text per title and per text, each with an exact 0/1 visibility (1 − min(1, |shown − i|)); the title is announced "Step N of M: <title>." and the "Step N of M" line is drawn on a canvas, so a screen reader hears it once

snippets.note: Back and Next write @step; play / pause writes playing, s0 and t0
the current step's title and text, switched by exact 0/1 visibility
@stepEased grows each square in; the accent dot slides
Step N of 4: <title>. on the title; Back, Play / Pause, Next labelled
the triangle and the three squares, drawn by the caller from @stepEased
"Step N of 4" from textFromFloat(shown + 1), drawn on the progress canvas and announced with the title

step.meaning: the step, 0-based (what Back, Next and Pause write)

check.describe: Step 1 of 4: a white 3-4-5 right triangle with a, b and c labels, the title "A right triangle" and two lines of text under it, a dimmed Back with a play triangle beside it, and Next on the right. Next (tap at 312, 440) shows "The square on a" and a blue square growing under side a with 9 in it; the next adds a purple square left of side b with 16; the last a green square tilted on the hypotenuse with 25, the text ending "So a² + b² = c²", and Next becomes Start over, which goes back to step 1. Play (105, 440) advances every 3 s, its icon becomes two bars (Pause), and stops on step 4; a tap on Back or Next while playing stops playing. step 3 renders the full figure. Mono: no play button (no motion), outlined Back, dots as grey rings with a white (black) current one. A screen reader hears "Step 1 of 4: A right triangle", the text, Back (disabled), Play and Next.

components.summary: The frame of a step-by-step explanation: the caller draws the explanation (in the `content` slot) from the current step, and the walkthrough shows that step's title and text, "Step N of M" with dots, Back and Next (Done on the last step), and optionally a play / pause button that advances one step every `interval` seconds. It publishes the live step and an eased copy of it for the drawing.
pitfalls: For a new explainer use StepExplainer: it adapts to size, has its own background, and takes computed step counts and captions. Walkthrough has a fixed count and static captions

The drawing must read `shown` or `eased`, not `step`: while autoplay plays, `step` stays where play started and the step on screen is computed from the clock. Pause, Back and Next write the step on screen back into `step`, so a paused walkthrough has step = shown

`shown` and `eased` are published as tree variables named after the variables you bind ({"$name": ...}): read them in the `content` slot or anywhere after the call in the document. Never declare them in resources as well: the resources variable wins and reads 0 (check_component's demo declares every @name a call references, so a sweep of a call whose content reads @stepEased draws step 0; check the drawing with the document instead). A reader before the call fails to convert (Variable not found)

Grow the k-th element of a drawing with clamp(0, 1, @stepEased - (k - 1)) (0 before step k, 1 after, easing in between), and fade its labels with the same value as paint alpha. Keep the drawing's own canvas variables out of resources too

Autoplay reads animationTime() (seconds since the player started the document), not the wall clock: shown = clamp(0, last, step + playing × (s0 + floor((animationTime() − t0) / interval) − step)). Play runs five actions in order: step = shown, step = 0 if not running and on the last step (play there starts over), s0 = step, t0 = animationTime(), playing = 1 − running. Running is playing × (shown < last), so the button shows Play again on the last step

No clock listener: frames while playing come from an animated local whose target, running × floor(animationTime() × 2), changes every half second (each change restarts a 0.75 s ease), so a PLAYING walkthrough repaints every frame and a paused or finished one is idle (inspect runtime: idle). check_component's lint warning "animationTime() alone never schedules a repaint" is expected: that local is what schedules it. A continuousSec() clock would keep the document repainting even while paused (TIM-14)

Playing does not survive a reload: t0 is relative to the player's animationTime, so a document reloaded with playing 1 times its steps from the load. Pass "playing": 1 to start playing at load; the first step comes after `interval`. A timed step runs no action and tells the host nothing: onStep, onNext and onBack run on taps only
Mono (mono-dark, mono-light) has no play button and no autoplay (no motion on e-ink or always-on displays), and `eased` is `shown` itself: the drawing snaps

The step on screen is clamp(0, last, round(step)): a host value out of range shows the first or last step. The caption is one text per title and per text, each with an exact 0/1 visibility 1 − min(1, |shown − i|); the title is announced "Step N of M: <title>" and the text after it. The "Step N of M" line is drawn on the progress canvas, so a screen reader does not hear it twice

With a `content` slot the walkthrough fills its parent (fillMaxSize) and the content takes the height the caption and controls leave: give it a parent with a height. Without `captionHeight` the caption takes the current step's height and everything above and below moves when the text length changes; with it, a longer text is clipped

Back is a Button with a runtime enabled (min(1, shown)), dimmed and inert on step 1. Next and the last step's button are two Buttons switched by visibility; the last one runs onDone, or without it reads Start over and goes back to step 1. A tap on Back or Next while playing stops playing. Every target is 48 dp tall
Give a hostNamedAction to onNext / onBack / onDone, never to onStep: a named action written in two click lists reaches the host by name from one of them only (Stepper)

A document variable named `step` hides the step() function in your own expressions (json2rc resolves the bare token as the variable, so step(x, e) becomes nonsense); this component avoids step() for that reason. Use min/max arithmetic, or name the variable otherwise
The dots are 7 dp at a 14 dp pitch, right-aligned, decorative (not tappable); past about 12 steps they crowd the "Step N of M" line
inspect pins animationTime() to its clock (seconds since 2026-01-01, which loses sub-second precision as a float): pin clock "2026-01-01T00:00:00" when checking autoplay with inspect interact

Expanded, never a pattern: it contains texts (U7) and declares named values. Each instance costs about 3.7 KB with three short steps and autoplay (3.0 KB without autoplay; mono about 3.8 KB, no play button) plus about 350 B per further step and the length of its strings, mostly in the three Buttons (Back has two faces for its runtime enabled)
loop: the eased step (eased) runs back from the last step to the first when the cycle wraps; a drawing that must jump forward at the wrap reads shown (the whole step) and its own phase

components.name: weather-icon
components.title: Weather icon
components.prompt: Draw weather symbols for sunny, cloudy, rain, snow and thunderstorm, without images or SVG paths, labelled underneath.
teaches: {"WeatherIcon": {"condition": "rain"}} draws a 48 dp symbol; condition is static (sun, cloud, rain, snow, storm, partly, fog) and size scales the 24-unit drawing
A cloud is three circles over a rounded rectangle; the mono outline is the same shapes drawn larger in onSurface and then in the background colour, which outlines their union
Sun rays are one line in a loop that rotates the canvas 45° per pass, so the paint is set once
night: "@isNight" swaps the sun for a crescent moon (sun and partly) at run time: both drawings are written, each in a conditionalOperations block on the variable
The crescent is a pathData op list of cubics (two circular arcs), about 200 B, so it needs no background-coloured bite and mono strokes the same path

{"WeatherIcon": {"morph": true, "value": "@cond"}} is one outline that morphs between sun, cloud, rain, snow and storm whenever @cond (0..4) changes: per-condition eased weights and four chained pathTweens, so any pair morphs directly
look "rich" gives gradient bodies and a sun glow for icons on a coloured sky; animate: true turns the rays and makes the rain fall, the snow drift and the bolt flicker (continuous repaint)
The morph outlines come from the weather-outline generator ($gen): one shared path per shape in the document, whatever the number of calls

snippets.note: sun: disc and eight rays from a rotate loop
rain: cloud of circles and a rounded rect, three slanted lines
storm at 32 dp with its own label
morph mode, driven by @wx; the box around it cycles @wx on tap
four chained pathTweens between the generator's outlines
one eased weight per condition

wx.meaning: the morphing icons' condition, 0 sun to 4 storm

check.describe: Five distinct 48 dp icons in equal columns, each labelled: an amber sun with eight rays, a grey cloud centred in its square, a cloud over three slanted blue drops, a cloud over three blue dots, and a cloud over an amber bolt; below, a 32 dp storm icon. In mono the sun is a ring with rays and the clouds are white outlines. The columns are weighted: at 260 dp they get closer, at 480 dp they spread out; the icons keep their size. Below: two 96 dp morph icons (flat on the background, rich on a blue sky tile, an outlined drawing in mono) showing the sun; tapping the first steps @wx (sun -> cloud -> rain -> snow -> storm), and both morph to it: mid-morph the disc swells into the cloud outline.

components.summary: A square weather symbol drawn with circles, rounded rectangles, lines and a crescent path: sun, cloud, rain, snow, storm, partly cloudy or fog, with a moon instead of the sun at night. Opt-in morph mode: one outline that morphs smoothly between sun, cloud, rain, snow and storm when a value changes, with optional animated rays, rain, snow and lightning.
pitfalls: condition is static: each condition is a different drawing written into the document. To show a condition the host chooses at run time, put one call per condition in a stateLayout (or behind visibility) driven by a host number: a float variable, which stateLayout reads as its index and a TextChoice for the condition word can read too (a TextChoice reads an integer variable as 0). night, by contrast, is read at run time: with a "@variable" both the sun and the moon are written, each in a conditionalOperations block (night < 0.5 draws the sun, >= 0.5 the moon)
No SVG paths: the cloud is three circles over a rounded rectangle, and the bolt three round-capped lines (an SVG path string costs about 4 KB in Java, padded to 1024 floats)

The moon is a crescent path (pathData from an op list of cubics, about 200 B), not an SVG string and not a disc with a background-coloured bite, so it sits on any surface; mono strokes the same path as an outline

Mono draws the cloud as an outline: the same shapes 1.25 units larger in onSurface, then the shapes themselves in @colors.background, so the ring follows their union. It assumes the icon sits on the background colour, which every surface is in mono
The sun's eight rays are one line drawn in a loop that rotates the canvas 45° per pass (8 × 45° = 360°, back to the start)
The drawing is scaled to the box the layout actually gives the canvas (min of its width and height, centred), so a call clamped by a smaller parent shrinks instead of being cut off
partly draws the small sun or moon first and the cloud over it: the filled cloud (or, in mono, its background-filled outline) hides the part behind it

Morph mode (morph: true) reads value (0 sun, 1 cloud, 2 rain, 3 snow, 4 storm) at run time: one call follows a host variable or a tap, no stateLayout needed. Each condition has an eased weight (anim of 1 - |value - i|) and four chained pathTweens give each outline its weight, so a change from a to b is a pure a-to-b morph. Fractions blend outlines (2.5 is half rain cloud, half snow cloud)

The five outlines are op-list paths from the weather-outline generator, written once per document (about 4.5 KB for the five, shared by every morph call); each morph call adds about 1.5 KB (flat) or 2 KB (rich) for the tweens and details. For a row of icons that never changes at run time, the static condition is much smaller

Morph mode names its variables wxw0..wxw4, wxt, wxp, wxq and wxf and its paths wxM1..wxM3 and wxBody: every call redefines them in its own canvas, so several calls coexist, but don't use those names in the document

animate repaints every frame while the icon is on screen (continuousSec); leave it off for widgets and lists. Mono is always still and has no morph motion (the expansion removes every anim): the outline switches

In morph mode size is still what the canvas asks for, and the drawing scales to the box it gets: to size it from an expression, put the call in a box whose width and height are that expression and give size a large value

components.name: world map
components.title: WorldMap
components.prompt: A world map with day and night and four cities, and a map of Europe with two countries highlighted and a marker the app moves.
teaches: Call it with a region and what to mark: {"WorldMap": {"cities": ["Tokyo"], "labels": true}}; region takes world, a continent, a country (ISO code) or a lon/lat box
night: true shades the night side from the clock (world maps)

For a world clock add twilight: true (a soft night edge), sun: true (the sun over the subsolar point) and daylight: true (city dots in dayColor with a halo where the sun is up, markerColor elsewhere; mono: filled or hollow)
markLon/markLat take host variables: one marker the app moves
{"$map"}, {"$mapHeight"} and {"$mapPoint"} are the building blocks for a map of your own in a canvas

check.describe: Top: a world in plate carrée at 10:30 on 31 October: the night side shaded with a soft edge, the sun over southern Africa, London lit (warm dot with a halo), New York, Tokyo and Sydney at night (red dots); bottom: Europe with borders, France and Germany in the primary colour and a marker on Paris (lon/lat host variables). evening (19:45): the day over the Americas, New York lit, London dark. Mono: the night edge as a line, the sun a disc in a ring, lit cities filled and the others hollow.

components.summary: A map of the world, a continent, a country or a frame fitted to a list of places (Natural Earth, public domain): land or countries with borders, highlighted countries, countries coloured through a ramp with a legend, city markers with labels, a route or several labelled legs, a marker from host lon/lat, and an optional day/night shade from the clock. It scales to fit the box it gets, and opt-in for a world clock: a soft twilight edge on the night shade, the sun over the subsolar point and city markers that light up where the sun is up.
pitfalls: Geometry is fixed when the document is built (region, detail, borders, highlight, cities, states, the route's ends); at run time the app can colour countries (values + valueCountries), move points (pointsLon/pointsLat arrays), move the marker (markLon/markLat), advance the route (progress) and the clock moves the night

night assumes the world box ("world": latitudes 84 to -58, plate carrée): on a continent or a country it is not drawn correctly; leave it off there. The night side is one filled pathExpression along the terminator (atan(-cos(H) / tan(declination)))

Bytes grow with detail and borders: a world of land at low detail is ~6 KB, countries ~10 KB; Europe with borders at medium ~28 KB; each valueCountries entry adds its own outline (Europe's 48 at low ~30 KB). Prefer land for a backdrop and borders only where they matter

For anything else at map coordinates draw in your own canvas inside the same translate/scale: {"$mapPoint": {"region": ..., "lon": "@lon", "lat": "@lat"}} (x; "axis": "y" for y), {"$mapHeight": region} (the box height for width 1000), {"$mapRoute": {region, from, to, axis: "path" | "x" | "y" | "angle"}} (a great circle, or its samples as an array for arraySpline(@array, t)). In your own canvas use {"$map": {..., "outline": true}} for a stroked coast (a clipped fill's straight edges would show)
In mono the land is an outline (no fills), the highlight a fill, the night a grey shade
It fills the width it is given (fillMaxWidth): beside other content in a row, give it a weight or a width, or the row's other children get nothing

A list region frames those places, not a continent: ["Dubai", "London", "Singapore"]. Name the legs' cities in it (or [from, to] pairs, which add the arc's bulge): an arc to a place outside the frame leaves the map, routes are not clipped

legs draws each leg's arc and end dots; labels and the hub's name come from cities + labels (draw them too, the leg labels avoid them). With region, a label is placed for a map about 300 dp wide at the given height and a much smaller map can crowd them; with fit, text scales with the map and labels that would collide at a small size are hidden

fit + fill is the map that follows the window: {"fit": ["Dubai", "London"], "fill": true} takes the column's remaining height (put it last or give its siblings fixed sizes) and frames the places at whatever size the window has; the geometry covers boxes from 0.9:1 to 2.6:1 (outside that, blank bands)

ramp needs values + valueCountries; the values are raw (valueMin..valueMax, e.g. 0..250 €/MWh), not 0..1. Start the ramp with a colour unlike the land (not @colors.track), or the lowest values read as no data. Use borders: true so neighbours of close values stay apart, and legend: true for the scale

A world clock: night + twilight + sun + daylight with cities is the whole map of SHW-21: the soft edge (three shades), the sun over the subsolar point and city dots that glow where the sun is up. All three new options assume the world box (region "world" or "world-full") and repaint once a minute with the clock; the subsolar longitude ignores the equation of time (up to 4 degrees)
